passages.original: Nor services to do, till you require.
passages.vernacular: 亦冇服務可做,直到你要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也沒服務可做,直到你要求。

passages.original:
Nor dare I chide the world-without-end hour,
Whilst I, my sovereign, watch the clock for you,
Nor think the bitterness of absence sour,
When you have bid your servant once adieu;
passages.vernacular: 我亦唔敢責備無盡嘅時辰,當我,我嘅君主,為你看住時鐘,亦唔敢覺得缺席嘅苦澀酸楚,當你向你嘅僕人道別之後;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不敢責備無盡的時辰,當我,我的君主,為你看著時鐘,也不敢覺得缺席的苦澀酸楚,當你向你的僕人道別之後;

passages.original:
Nor dare I question with my jealous thought
Where you may be, or your affairs suppose,
But, like a sad slave, stay and think of nought
Save, where you are, how happy you make those.
passages.vernacular: 我亦唔敢用我妒忌嘅思想質問你可能喺邊,或猜測你嘅事務,而係好似悲傷嘅奴隸,留低,什麼都不想,除咗你在哪裡,你令那些人幾快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不敢用我妒忌的思想質問你可能在哪,或猜測你的事務,而是像悲傷的奴隸,留下,什麼都不想,除了你在哪裡,你使那些人多快樂。

passages.original:
So true a fool is love, that in your will,
Though you do anything, he thinks no ill.
passages.vernacular: 愛係咁真誠嘅傻瓜,在你嘅意志中,雖然你做任何事,佢都唔覺得有惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛是這樣真誠的傻瓜,在你的意志中,雖然你做任何事,他都不覺得有惡。

passages.title: Sonnet 58
passages.original:
That god forbid, that made me first your slave,
I should in thought control your times of pleasure,
Or at your hand the account of hours to crave,
Being your vassal, bound to stay your leisure!
passages.vernacular: 願那使我最初成為你奴隸嘅神阻止,我竟然在思想上控制你享樂嘅時間,或向你要求時辰嘅賬目,身為你嘅家臣,必須等候你嘅閒暇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願那使我最初成為你奴隸的神阻止,我竟然在思想上控制你享樂的時間,或向你要求時辰的賬目,身為你的家臣,必須等候你的閒暇!

passages.original:
O! let me suffer, being at your beck,
The imprison’d absence of your liberty;
passages.vernacular: 啊!讓我受苦,聽你召喚,受你自由嘅被囚禁缺席;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!讓我受苦,聽你召喚,受你自由的被囚禁缺席;

passages.original:
And patience, tame to sufferance, bide each check,
Without accusing you of injury.
passages.vernacular: 耐心被馴服於忍受,忍受每一次責難,不指控你傷害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耐心被馴服於忍受,忍受每一次責難,不指控你傷害。

passages.original:
Be where you list, your charter is so strong
That you yourself may privilage your time
To what you will; to you it doth belong
Yourself to pardon of self-doing crime.
passages.vernacular: 你喜歡在邊就喺邊,你嘅特許狀咁強,以致你可以自己將你嘅時間特許畀你想要嘅;佢屬於你,自己赦免自己所犯嘅罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你喜歡在哪就在哪,你的特許狀這麼強,以致你可以自己將你的時間特許給你想要的;它屬於你,自己赦免自己所犯的罪。

passages.original:
I am to wait, though waiting so be hell,
Not blame your pleasure be it ill or well.
passages.vernacular: 我要等待,雖然咁樣等待係地獄,不責備你嘅歡愉,無論好壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要等待,雖然這樣等待是地獄,不責備你的歡愉,無論好壞。

passages.title: Sonnet 59
passages.original:
If there be nothing new, but that which is
Hath been before, how are our brains beguil’d,
Which labouring for invention bear amiss
The second burthen of a former child!
passages.vernacular: 如果冇新嘢,現存嘅一切以前都有過,我哋嘅頭腦點樣被欺騙,為創作而勞碌,錯誤地承受先前孩子嘅第二個重擔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果沒新東西,現存的一切以前都有過,我們的頭腦怎樣被欺騙,為創作而勞碌,錯誤地承受先前孩子的第二個重擔!

passages.original:
O! that record could with a backward look,
Even of five hundred courses of the sun,
Show me your image in some antique book,
Since mind at first in character was done!
passages.vernacular: 啊!願記錄可以回望,甚至五百個太陽運行,在某本古書中向我展示你嘅形象,因為思想最初就被寫成文字!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!願記錄可以回望,甚至五百個太陽運行,在某本古書中向我展示你的形象,因為思想最初就被寫成文字!

passages.original:
That I might see what the old world could say
To this composed wonder of your frame;
passages.vernacular: 好讓我睇到舊世界對你軀體呢個構成嘅奇蹟會講咩;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好讓我看到舊世界對你軀體這個構成的奇蹟會說什麼;

passages.original:
Wh’r we are mended, or wh’r better they,
Or whether revolution be the same.
passages.vernacular: 我哋有冇進步,或者佢哋更好,或者循環係咪一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們有沒有進步,或者他們更好,或者循環是不是一樣。

passages.original:
O! sure I am the wits of former days,
To subjects worse have given admiring praise.
passages.vernacular: 啊!我肯定從前嘅才智之士,對較差嘅題材都給過讚嘆嘅讚美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!我肯定從前的才智之士,對較差的題材都給過讚嘆的讚美。

passages.title: Sonnet 60
passages.original:
Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore,
So do our minutes hasten to their end;
passages.vernacular: 好似波浪向鋪滿卵石嘅海岸湧去,我哋嘅分鐘也趕向佢哋嘅終點;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像波浪向鋪滿卵石的海岸湧去,我們的分鐘也趕向它們的終點;

passages.original:
Each changing place with that which goes before,
In sequent toil all forwards do contend.
passages.vernacular: 每個同前面離開嘅交換位置,在接連嘅辛勞中全部向前爭取。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個與前面離開的交換位置,在接連的辛勞中全部向前爭取。

passages.original:
Nativity, once in the main of light,
Crawls to maturity, wherewith being crown’d,
Crooked eclipses ’gainst his glory fight,
And Time that gave doth now his gift confound.
passages.vernacular: 誕生,一度在光明嘅大海中,爬向成熟,在成熟中被加冕,彎曲嘅蝕對抗佢嘅榮耀,賦予嘅時間而家毀滅佢嘅禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誕生,一度在光明的大海中,爬向成熟,在成熟中被加冕,彎曲的蝕對抗他的榮耀,賦予的時間現在毀滅他的禮物。

passages.original:
Time doth transfix the flourish set on youth
And delves the parallels in beauty’s brow,
Feeds on the rarities of nature’s truth,
And nothing stands but for his scythe to mow:
passages.vernacular: 時間刺穿放在青春上嘅繁盛,在美貌額頭上挖出平行線,以大自然真理嘅珍品為食,冇嘢站得住,只為佢嘅鐮刀割:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間刺穿放在青春上的繁盛,在美貌額頭上挖出平行線,以大自然真理的珍品為食,沒東西站得住,只為他的鐮刀割:

passages.original: And yet to times in hope, my verse shall stand.
passages.vernacular: 不過為咗未來嘅時代,我嘅詩會屹立,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過為了未來的時代,我的詩會屹立,

passages.original: Praising thy worth, despite his cruel hand.
passages.vernacular: 讚美你嘅價值,不顧佢殘酷嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讚美你的價值,不顧他殘酷的手。

passages.title: Sonnet 61
passages.original:
Is it thy will, thy image should keep open
My heavy eyelids to the weary night?
passages.vernacular: 係咪你嘅意志,令你嘅形象令我沉重嘅眼皮在疲憊嘅夜晚保持睜開?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是不是你的意志,使你的形象使我沉重的眼皮在疲憊的夜晚保持睜開?

passages.original:
Dost thou desire my slumbers should be broken,
While shadows like to thee do mock my sight?
passages.vernacular: 你想我嘅睡眠被打斷,當似你嘅影子嘲弄我嘅視野?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想我的睡眠被打斷,當像你的影子嘲弄我的視野?

passages.original:
Is it thy spirit that thou send’st from thee
So far from home into my deeds to pry,
To find out shames and idle hours in me,
The scope and tenure of thy jealousy?
passages.vernacular: 係咪你嘅靈魂,你從你處差遣咁遠離家,到我嘅行為中窺探,找出我身上嘅羞恥同閒散時間,你妒忌嘅範圍同期限?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是不是你的靈魂,你從你處差遣這麼遠離家,到我的行為中窺探,找出我身上的羞恥和閒散時間,你妒忌的範圍和期限?

passages.original: O, no! thy love, though much, is not so great:
passages.vernacular: 啊,不!你嘅愛,雖然多,冇咁大:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,不!你的愛,雖然多,沒這麼大:

passages.original: It is my love that keeps mine eye awake:
passages.vernacular: 係我嘅愛令我嘅眼睛保持清醒:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我的愛使我的眼睛保持清醒:

passages.original:
Mine own true love that doth my rest defeat,
To play the watchman ever for thy sake:
passages.vernacular: 我自己真誠嘅愛擊敗我嘅休息,為咗你嘅緣故永遠做守夜人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己真誠的愛擊敗我的休息,為了你的緣故永遠做守夜人:

passages.original:
For thee watch I, whilst thou dost wake elsewhere,
From me far off, with others all too near.
passages.vernacular: 我為你守夜,而你喺別處醒住,離我好遠,同其他人太近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為你守夜,而你在別處醒著,離我很遠,與其他人太近。

passages.title: Sonnet 62
passages.original:
Sin of self-love possesseth all mine eye
And all my soul, and all my every part;
passages.vernacular: 自愛嘅罪佔有我所有嘅眼睛同我所有嘅靈魂,同我每一個部分;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自愛的罪佔有我所有的眼睛和我所有的靈魂,和我每一個部分;

passages.original:
And for this sin there is no remedy,
It is so grounded inward in my heart.
passages.vernacular: 而呢個罪冇補救,佢如此深植喺我嘅心裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而這個罪沒補救,它如此深植在我的心裡。

passages.original:
Methinks no face so gracious is as mine,
No shape so true, no truth of such account;
passages.vernacular: 我覺得冇一張臉似我咁優雅,冇一個形體咁真,冇一個真理咁有分量;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得沒一張臉像我這麼優雅,沒一個形體這麼真,沒一個真理這麼有分量;

passages.original:
And for myself mine own worth do define,
As I all other in all worths surmount.
passages.vernacular: 為我自己,我自己界定我嘅價值,好似我在所有價值中超越所有其他人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為我自己,我自己界定我的價值,好像我在所有價值中超越所有其他人。

passages.vernacular: 不過當我嘅鏡子真正向我展示自己,被曬黑嘅古老歲月打擊同砍削,我讀到我自己嘅自愛完全相反;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當我的鏡子真正向我展示自己,被曬黑的古老歲月打擊和砍削,我讀到我自己的自愛完全相反;

passages.original: Self so self-loving were iniquity.
passages.vernacular: 咁自愛嘅自我會係罪惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣自愛的自我會是罪惡。

passages.original:
’Tis thee, myself, that for myself I praise,
Painting my age with beauty of thy days.
passages.vernacular: 係你,我自己,我為咗我自己而讚美,用你青春嘅美貌塗畫我嘅年老。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是你,我自己,我為了我自己而讚美,用你青春的美貌塗畫我的年老。

passages.title: Sonnet 63
passages.original:
Against my love shall be as I am now,
With Time’s injurious hand crush’d and o’erworn;
passages.vernacular: 為咗我嘅愛人會好似我而家咁,被時間有害嘅手壓碎同磨損;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了我的愛人會好像我現在這樣,被時間有害的手壓碎和磨損;

passages.vernacular: 當時辰抽乾佢嘅血,用線條同皺紋填滿佢嘅額頭;當佢青春嘅早晨已行向年老陡峭嘅夜晚;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當時辰抽乾他的血,用線條和皺紋填滿他的額頭;當他青春的早晨已行向年老陡峭的夜晚;

passages.vernacular: 而佢而家為王嘅所有美貌,正在消逝,或已消逝出視線,偷走佢春天嘅寶藏;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而他現在為王的所有美貌,正在消逝,或已消逝出視線,偷走他春天的寶藏;

passages.original:
For such a time do I now fortify
Against confounding age’s cruel knife,
That he shall never cut from memory
My sweet love’s beauty, though my lover’s life:
passages.vernacular: 為咗咁嘅時刻,我而家築起防禦,對抗毀滅一切嘅年老殘酷嘅刀,令佢永遠不能從記憶中割走我甜美愛人嘅美貌,雖然我愛人嘅生命會被割:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了這樣的時刻,我現在築起防禦,對抗毀滅一切的年老殘酷的刀,使他永遠不能從記憶中割走我甜美愛人的美貌,雖然我愛人的生命會被割:

passages.original:
His beauty shall in these black lines be seen,
And they shall live, and he in them still green.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅美貌會喺呢啲黑色嘅線條中被見到,佢哋會活下去,而佢喺佢哋之中仍然青翠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的美貌會在這些黑色的線條中被看到,它們會活下去,而他在它們之中仍然青翠。

passages.title: Sonnet 64
passages.original:
When I have seen by Time’s fell hand defac’d
The rich-proud cost of outworn buried age;
passages.vernacular: 當我見到被時間兇殘之手毀壞嘅,衰老埋葬嘅富麗驕傲嘅花費;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我看到被時間兇殘之手毀壞的,衰老埋葬的富麗驕傲的花費;

passages.original:
When sometime lofty towers I see down-raz’d,
And brass eternal slave to mortal rage;
passages.vernacular: 當我見到曾經高聳嘅塔被夷平,永恆嘅銅成為凡人狂怒嘅奴隸;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我看到曾經高聳的塔被夷平,永恆的銅成為凡人狂怒的奴隸;

passages.original:
When I have seen the hungry ocean gain
Advantage on the kingdom of the shore,
And the firm soil win of the watery main,
Increasing store with loss, and loss with store;
passages.vernacular: 當我見到饑餓嘅大海取得對海岸王國嘅優勢,而穩固嘅土地贏取水汪汪嘅大海,以損失增加儲備,以儲備增加損失;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我看到饑餓的大海取得對海岸王國的優勢,而穩固的土地贏取水汪汪的大海,以損失增加儲備,以儲備增加損失;

passages.original:
When I have seen such interchange of state,
Or state itself confounded, to decay;
passages.vernacular: 當我見到咁樣嘅狀態交換,或狀態本身被混淆到衰敗;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我看到這樣的狀態交換,或狀態本身被混淆到衰敗;

passages.original: Ruin hath taught me thus to ruminate:
passages.vernacular: 毀滅教我咁樣反覆思量:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毀滅教我這樣反覆思量:

passages.original: That Time will come and take my love away.
passages.vernacular: 時間會來,將我嘅愛人帶走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間會來,將我的愛人帶走。

passages.original:
This thought is as a death which cannot choose
But weep to have, that which it fears to lose.
passages.vernacular: 呢個念頭好似死亡,不能選擇,只能為擁有佢所怕失去嘅而哭泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個念頭好像死亡,不能選擇,只能為擁有它所怕失去的而哭泣。

passages.title: Sonnet 65
passages.original:
Since brass, nor stone, nor earth, nor boundless sea,
But sad mortality o’ersways their power,
How with this rage shall beauty hold a plea,
Whose action is no stronger than a flower?
passages.vernacular: 既然銅、石、土、無邊嘅海,都被悲傷嘅死亡統治佢哋嘅力量,美貌憑呢種狂怒點樣提出申辯,佢嘅行動並唔比一朵花更強?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然銅、石、土、無邊的海,都被悲傷的死亡統治它們的力量,美貌憑這種狂怒怎樣提出申辯,它的行動並不比一朵花更強?

passages.original:
O! how shall summer’s honey breath hold out,
Against the wrackful siege of battering days,
When rocks impregnable are not so stout,
Nor gates of steel so strong but Time decays?
passages.vernacular: 啊!夏天蜜糖般嘅氣息點樣抵擋猛擊嘅日子嘅毀滅性圍攻,當堅不可摧嘅岩石都唔夠堅硬,鋼門都唔夠強,時間都會腐蝕?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!夏天蜜糖般的氣息怎樣抵擋猛擊的日子的毀滅性圍攻,當堅不可摧的岩石都不夠堅硬,鋼門都不夠強,時間都會腐蝕?

passages.original:
O fearful meditation! where, alack,
Shall Time’s best jewel from Time’s chest lie hid?
passages.vernacular: 啊可怕嘅沉思!唉,時間最好嘅珠寶,可以喺時間嘅箱子裡藏喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊可怕的沉思!唉,時間最好的珠寶,可以在時間的箱子裡藏在哪?

passages.original: Or what strong hand can hold his swift foot back?
passages.vernacular: 或者邊隻強大嘅手可以拉住佢迅疾嘅腳?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者哪隻強大的手可以拉住他迅疾的腳?

passages.original: Or who his spoil of beauty can forbid?
passages.vernacular: 或者邊個可以禁止佢掠奪美貌?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者誰可以禁止他掠奪美貌?

passages.original:
O! none, unless this miracle have might,
That in black ink my love may still shine bright.
passages.vernacular: 啊!冇人,除非呢個奇蹟有力量,令我嘅愛人在黑色嘅墨水中仍然明亮地閃耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!沒人,除非這個奇蹟有力量,使我的愛人在黑色的墨水中仍然明亮地閃耀。

passages.title: Sonnet 66
passages.original: Tired with all these, for restful death I cry:
passages.vernacular: 厭倦了所有這些,我為安息嘅死亡呼喊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 厭倦了所有這些,我為安息的死亡呼喊:

passages.original:
As to behold desert a beggar born,
And needy nothing trimm’d in jollity,
And purest faith unhappily forsworn,
And gilded honour shamefully misplac’d,
And maiden virtue rudely strumpeted,
And right perfection wrongfully disgrac’d,
And strength by limping sway disabled
And art made tongue-tied by authority,
And folly, doctor-like, controlling skill,
And simple truth miscall’d simplicity,
And captive good attending captain ill:
passages.vernacular: 看到功績生為乞丐,貧乏嘅空虛被裝飾得歡樂,最純潔嘅信仰被不幸地背棄,鍍金嘅榮譽被可恥地錯放,少女嘅貞潔被粗暴地玷污成娼妓,正確嘅完美被錯誤地羞辱,力量被跛腳嘅統治削弱,技藝被權威封口,愚蠢像博士般控制技能,簡單嘅真被誤稱為愚蠢,被俘嘅善服侍統帥嘅惡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到功績生為乞丐,貧乏的空虛被裝飾得歡樂,最純潔的信仰被不幸地背棄,鍍金的榮譽被可恥地錯放,少女的貞潔被粗暴地玷污成娼妓,正確的完美被錯誤地羞辱,力量被跛腳的統治削弱,技藝被權威封口,愚蠢像博士般控制技能,簡單的真被誤稱為愚蠢,被俘的善服侍統帥的惡:

passages.original:
Tir’d with all these, from these would I be gone,
Save that, to die, I leave my love alone.
passages.vernacular: 厭倦了所有這些,我想離開這些,只是,一死,我就將我嘅愛人獨自留低。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 厭倦了所有這些,我想離開這些,只是,一死,我就將我的愛人獨自留下。

passages.title: Sonnet 67
passages.original:
Ah! wherefore with infection should he live,
And with his presence grace impiety,
That sin by him advantage should achieve,
And lace itself with his society?
passages.vernacular: 啊!佢點解要帶住感染而活,用佢嘅存在為不敬增光,令罪藉佢取得優勢,並用佢嘅交往裝飾自己?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!他為什麼要帶著感染而活,用他的存在為不敬增光,使罪藉他取得優勢,並用他的交往裝飾自己?

passages.original:
Why should false painting imitate his cheek,
And steel dead seeming of his living hue?
passages.vernacular: 點解虛假嘅化妝要模仿佢嘅臉頰,偷取佢活生生膚色嘅死寂外表?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼虛假的化妝要模仿他的臉頰,偷取他活生生膚色的死寂外表?

passages.original:
Why should poor beauty indirectly seek
Roses of shadow, since his rose is true?
passages.vernacular: 點解可憐嘅美貌要間接尋求影子般嘅玫瑰,既然佢嘅玫瑰係真嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼可憐的美貌要間接尋求影子般的玫瑰,既然他的玫瑰是真的?

passages.original:
Why should he live, now Nature bankrupt is,
Beggar’d of blood to blush through lively veins?
passages.vernacular: 既然大自然破產,連令生動血管泛紅嘅血都乞討不到,點解佢要活下去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然大自然破產,連使生動血管泛紅的血都乞討不到,為什麼他要活下去?

passages.original:
For she hath no exchequer now but his,
And proud of many, lives upon his gains.
passages.vernacular: 因為佢而家除咗佢嘅,冇別嘅國庫,驕傲於許多人,靠佢嘅收益生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為她現在除了他的,沒別的國庫,驕傲於許多人,靠他的收益生活。

passages.original:
O! him she stores, to show what wealth she had
In days long since, before these last so bad.
passages.vernacular: 啊!佢儲存佢,展示佢好耐之前曾有幾多財富,在呢啲最後咁壞嘅日子之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!她儲存他,展示她很久之前曾有多少財富,在這些最後這麼壞的日子之前。

passages.title: Sonnet 68
passages.original:
Thus is his cheek the map of days outworn,
When beauty lived and died as flowers do now,
Before these bastard signs of fair were born,
Or durst inhabit on a living brow;
passages.vernacular: 所以佢嘅臉頰係已磨損日子嘅地圖,當時美貌像而家嘅花一樣生同死,在呢啲美嘅私生標記出生之前,或敢居住在活嘅額頭之前;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他的臉頰是已磨損日子的地圖,當時美貌像現在的花一樣生和死,在這些美的私生標記出生之前,或敢居住在活的額頭之前;

passages.vernacular: 在死者嘅金色髮束(墳墓嘅權利)被剪走,在第二個頭上過第二次生命之前;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在死者的金色髮束(墳墓的權利)被剪走,在第二個頭上過第二次生命之前;

passages.original: Ere beauty’s dead fleece made another gay:
passages.vernacular: 在美貌嘅死羊毛令另一個人光鮮之前:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在美貌的死羊毛使另一個人光鮮之前:

passages.original:
In him those holy antique hours are seen,
Without all ornament, itself and true,
Making no summer of another’s green,
Robbing no old to dress his beauty new;
passages.vernacular: 在佢身上見到嗰啲神聖古老嘅時辰,冇任何裝飾,本真,不將別人嘅綠意當作自己嘅夏天,不搶劫舊嘅來裝扮佢新嘅美:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他身上看到那些神聖古老的時辰,沒任何裝飾,本真,不將別人的綠意當作自己的夏天,不搶劫舊的來裝扮他新的美:

passages.original:
And him as for a map doth Nature store,
To show false Art what beauty was of yore.
passages.vernacular: 大自然儲存佢好似一幅地圖,向虛假嘅藝術展示昔日嘅美貌係咩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大自然儲存他好像一幅地圖,向虛假的藝術展示昔日的美貌是什麼。

passages.title: Sonnet 69
passages.original:
Those parts of thee that the world’s eye doth view
Want nothing that the thought of hearts can mend;
passages.vernacular: 你身上世界之眼睇到嘅部分,冇任何欠缺,是心嘅思想可以改進嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你身上世界之眼看到的部分,沒任何欠缺,是心的思想可以改進的;

passages.original:
All tongues, the voice of souls, give thee that due,
Uttering bare truth, even so as foes commend.
passages.vernacular: 所有舌頭,靈魂嘅聲音,畀你應得嘅,說出赤裸嘅真,甚至敵人都咁稱讚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有舌頭,靈魂的聲音,給你應得的,說出赤裸的真,甚至敵人都這樣稱讚。

passages.original: Thy outward thus with outward praise is crown’d;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅外表就咁用外在嘅讚美加冕;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的外表就這樣用外在的讚美加冕;

passages.original:
But those same tongues, that give thee so thine own,
In other accents do this praise confound
By seeing farther than the eye hath shown.
passages.vernacular: 不過同一啲舌頭,畀你應得嘅,用另一種口音混淆呢個讚美,因為看得比眼睛所示更遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過同一些舌頭,給你應得的,用另一種口音混淆這個讚美,因為看得比眼睛所示更遠。

passages.original:
They look into the beauty of thy mind,
And that in guess they measure by thy deeds;
passages.vernacular: 佢哋望入你心靈嘅美,並憑你嘅行為去猜測衡量;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們望進你心靈的美,並憑你的行為去猜測衡量;

passages.original:
Then churls their thoughts, although their eyes were kind,
To thy fair flower add the rank smell of weeds:
passages.vernacular: 然後吝嗇鬼般嘅思想,雖然佢哋嘅眼睛友善,為你美麗嘅花添上雜草嘅腐臭:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後吝嗇鬼般的思想,雖然他們的眼睛友善,為你美麗的花添上雜草的腐臭:

passages.original:
But why thy odour matcheth not thy show,
The soil is this, that thou dost common grow.
passages.vernacular: 不過點解你嘅香氣同你嘅外表唔匹配,原因係呢個:你變得普通。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過為什麼你的香氣和你的外表不匹配,原因是這個:你變得普通。

passages.title: Sonnet 70
passages.original:
That thou art blam’d shall not be thy defect,
For slander’s mark was ever yet the fair;
passages.vernacular: 你被責備唔會係你嘅缺點,因為誹謗嘅目標向來係美;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你被責備不會是你的缺點,因為誹謗的目標向來是美;

passages.original:
The ornament of beauty is suspect,
A crow that flies in heaven’s sweetest air.
passages.vernacular: 美貌嘅裝飾被猜疑,係喺天上最甜美嘅空氣中飛嘅烏鴉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美貌的裝飾被猜疑,是在天上最甜美的空氣中飛的烏鴉。

passages.original:
So thou be good, slander doth but approve
Thy worth the greater being woo’d of time;
passages.vernacular: 只要你好,誹謗只會證明你嘅價值因被時間追求而更大;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要你好,誹謗只會證明你的價值因被時間追求而更大;

passages.original:
For canker vice the sweetest buds doth love,
And thou present’st a pure unstained prime.
passages.vernacular: 因為蛀蟲般嘅惡喜愛最甜美嘅花蕾,而你呈現純潔無污嘅盛年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為蛀蟲般的惡喜愛最甜美的花蕾,而你呈現純潔無污的盛年。

passages.original:
Thou hast passed by the ambush of young days
Either not assail’d, or victor being charg’d;
passages.vernacular: 你已經走過年輕日子嘅伏擊,不是未被攻擊,就是被攻擊時得勝;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你已經走過年輕日子的伏擊,不是未被攻擊,就是被攻擊時得勝;

passages.original:
Yet this thy praise cannot be so thy praise,
To tie up envy, evermore enlarg’d,
If some suspect of ill mask’d not thy show,
Then thou alone kingdoms of hearts shouldst owe.
passages.vernacular: 不過你呢個讚美唔能夠咁成為你嘅讚美,去綁住不斷擴大嘅嫉妒,如果某種對惡嘅猜疑冇遮住你嘅外表,咁你獨自就應該擁有心嘅王國。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你這個讚美不能夠這樣成為你的讚美,去綁住不斷擴大的嫉妒,如果某種對惡的猜疑沒遮住你的外表,那你獨自就應該擁有心的王國。

passages.title: Sonnet 71
passages.original:
No longer mourn for me when I am dead
Than you shall hear the surly sullen bell
Give warning to the world that I am fled
From this vile world with vilest worms to dwell:
passages.vernacular: 我死後,為我哀悼唔好超過你聽到陰沉嘅喪鐘,警告世界我已從這個卑劣嘅世界逃走,同最卑劣嘅蟲一齊居住嗰陣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我死後,為我哀悼不要超過你聽到陰沉的喪鐘,警告世界我已從這個卑劣的世界逃走,與最卑劣的蟲一起居住那時:

passages.original:
Nay, if you read this line, remember not
The hand that writ it, for I love you so,
That I in your sweet thoughts would be forgot,
If thinking on me then should make you woe.
passages.vernacular: 不,如果你讀呢行詩,唔好記得寫佢嘅手,因為我愛你咁深,以致寧願在你甜美嘅思想中被忘記,如果想起我會令你悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,如果你讀這行詩,不要記得寫它的手,因為我愛你這麼深,以致寧願在你甜美的思想中被忘記,如果想起我會使你悲傷。

passages.vernacular: 啊,我講,如果你望住呢首詩,當我也許已同黏土混合,連我可憐嘅名字都唔好複述;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我說,如果你望著這首詩,當我也許已與黏土混合,連我可憐的名字都不要複述;

passages.original: But let your love even with my life decay;
passages.vernacular: 讓你嘅愛甚至隨我嘅生命一齊衰亡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓你的愛甚至隨我的生命一起衰亡;

passages.original:
Lest the wise world should look into your moan,
And mock you with me after I am gone.
passages.vernacular: 免得聰明嘅世界察看你嘅哀悼,在我離去後同我一齊嘲笑你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 免得聰明的世界察看你的哀悼,在我離去後與我一起嘲笑你。

passages.title: Sonnet 72
passages.original:
O! lest the world should task you to recite
What merit lived in me, that you should love
After my death, dear love, forget me quite,
For you in me can nothing worthy prove;
passages.vernacular: 啊!免得世界要你背誦我身上有咩價值,令你應該在我死後愛我,親愛嘅愛人,完全忘記我,因為你在我身上證明不到任何值得嘅東西;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!免得世界要你背誦我身上有什麼價值,使你應該在我死後愛我,親愛的愛人,完全忘記我,因為你在我身上證明不到任何值得的東西;

passages.original:
Unless you would devise some virtuous lie,
To do more for me than mine own desert,
And hang more praise upon deceased I
Than niggard truth would willingly impart:
passages.vernacular: 除非你想出某個有德嘅謊言,為我做比我自己功績更多嘅,在亡故嘅我身上掛更多讚美,多過吝嗇嘅真願意給予嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除非你想出某個有德的謊言,為我做比我自己功績更多的,在亡故的我身上掛更多讚美,多過吝嗇的真願意給予的:

passages.original:
O! lest your true love may seem false in this
That you for love speak well of me untrue,
My name be buried where my body is,
And live no more to shame nor me nor you.
passages.vernacular: 啊!免得你真誠嘅愛在這點上顯得虛假,即你為愛而不真實咁講我好,讓我嘅名字埋葬在我身體所在嘅地方,不再活著令我或你蒙羞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!免得你真誠的愛在這點上顯得虛假,即你為愛而不真實地說我好,讓我的名字埋葬在我身體所在的地方,不再活著使我或你蒙羞。

passages.original:
For I am shamed by that which I bring forth,
And so should you, to love things nothing worth.
passages.vernacular: 因為我為我所帶來嘅東西羞愧,你也應該,為愛冇價值嘅東西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我為我所帶來的東西羞愧,你也應該,為愛沒價值的東西。

passages.title: Sonnet 73
passages.original:
That time of year thou mayst in me behold
When yellow leaves, or none, or few, do hang
Upon those boughs which shake against the cold,
Bare ruin’d choirs, where late the sweet birds sang.
passages.vernacular: 你可以喺我身上看到一年中呢個時節,當黃葉,冇或者疏落,掛在向寒冷顫抖嘅枝上,光禿荒廢嘅唱詩席,前不久甜美嘅鳥在那裡唱歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以在我身上看到一年中這個時節,當黃葉,沒或者疏落,掛在向寒冷顫抖的枝上,光禿荒廢的唱詩席,前不久甜美的鳥在那裡唱歌。

passages.original:
In me thou see’st the twilight of such day
As after sunset fadeth in the west;
passages.vernacular: 你喺我身上見到呢種日子嘅黃昏,在日落後喺西邊褪去;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在我身上看到這種日子的黃昏,在日落後在西邊褪去;

passages.original:
Which by and by black night doth take away,
Death’s second self, that seals up all in rest.
passages.vernacular: 隨後黑夜將佢帶走,死亡嘅第二個自己,將一切封入休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨後黑夜將它帶走,死亡的第二個自己,將一切封入休息。

passages.original:
In me thou see’st the glowing of such fire,
That on the ashes of his youth doth lie,
As the death-bed, whereon it must expire,
Consum’d with that which it was nourish’d by.
passages.vernacular: 你喺我身上見到呢種火嘅輝光,躺喺佢青春嘅灰燼上,好似佢必須熄滅嘅臨終床,被佢賴以滋養嘅消耗殆盡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在我身上看到這種火的輝光,躺在他青春的灰燼上,好像他必須熄滅的臨終床,被他賴以滋養的消耗殆盡。

passages.original:
This thou perceiv’st, which makes thy love more strong,
To love that well, which thou must leave ere long.
passages.vernacular: 你察覺到這點,令你嘅愛更強,好好愛你不久就必須離開嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你察覺到這點,使你的愛更強,好好愛你不久就必須離開的。

passages.title: Sonnet 74
passages.original:
But be contented: when that fell arrest
Without all bail shall carry me away,
My life hath in this line some interest,
Which for memorial still with thee shall stay.
passages.vernacular: 不過滿足吧:當嗰場殘酷嘅逮捕,無法保釋咁將我帶走,我嘅生命在這行詩中有某種權益,仍然留喺你身邊作紀念。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過滿足吧:當那場殘酷的逮捕,無法保釋地將我帶走,我的生命在這行詩中有某種權益,仍然留在你身邊作紀念。

passages.original:
When thou reviewest this, thou dost review
The very part was consecrate to thee:
passages.vernacular: 當你重溫這個,你重溫嘅正係獻畀你嘅部分:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你重溫這個,你重溫的正是獻給你的部分:

passages.original: The earth can have but earth, which is his due;
passages.vernacular: 大地只可以擁有泥土,這是佢應得嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大地只可以擁有泥土,這是她應得的;

passages.original: My spirit is thine, the better part of me:
passages.vernacular: 我嘅靈魂屬於你,係我更好嘅部分:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的靈魂屬於你,是我更好的部分:

passages.original:
So then thou hast but lost the dregs of life,
The prey of worms, my body being dead;
passages.vernacular: 所以你只是失去生命嘅渣滓,蟲嘅獵物,我嘅身體死咗;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你只是失去生命的渣滓,蟲的獵物,我的身體死了;

passages.original:
The coward conquest of a wretch’s knife,
Too base of thee to be remembered.
passages.vernacular: 一個可憐人嘅刀嘅懦弱勝利,對你嚟講太卑賤,不值得被記住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個可憐人的刀的懦弱勝利,對你來說太卑賤,不值得被記住。

passages.original:
The worth of that is that which it contains,
And that is this, and this with thee remains.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅價值就係佢所包含嘅,而那就係這個,這個與你同在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的價值就是它所包含的,而那就是這個,這個與你同在。

passages.title: Sonnet 75
passages.original:
So are you to my thoughts as food to life,
Or as sweet-season’d showers are to the ground;
passages.vernacular: 你對我嘅思想就似食物對生命,或似甜美調和嘅陣雨對大地;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對我的思想就像食物對生命,或像甜美調和的陣雨對大地;

passages.original:
And for the peace of you I hold such strife
As ’twixt a miser and his wealth is found.
passages.vernacular: 為咗你嘅平安,我持有咁嘅鬥爭,好似守財奴同佢財富之間所見嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了你的平安,我持有這樣的鬥爭,好像守財奴和他財富之間所見的。

passages.original:
Now proud as an enjoyer, and anon
Doubting the filching age will steal his treasure;
passages.vernacular: 而家驕傲得似享受者,隨即懷疑偷竊嘅年月會偷走佢嘅寶藏;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在驕傲得像享受者,隨即懷疑偷竊的年月會偷走他的寶藏;

passages.original:
Now counting best to be with you alone,
Then better’d that the world may see my pleasure:
passages.vernacular: 而家認為最好同你獨處,然後又覺得最好讓世界見到我嘅歡愉:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在認為最好與你獨處,然後又覺得最好讓世界看到我的歡愉:

passages.original:
Sometime all full with feasting on your sight,
And by and by clean starved for a look;
passages.vernacular: 有時喺望住你嘅景象中飽足,隨即為一瞥餓得要死;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時在望著你的景象中飽足,隨即為一瞥餓得要死;

passages.original:
Possessing or pursuing no delight,
Save what is had, or must from you be took.
passages.vernacular: 除咗已得到或必須從你取得嘅,我既唔擁有亦唔追求任何歡愉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了已得到或必須從你取得的,我既不擁有也不追求任何歡愉。

passages.original:
Thus do I pine and surfeit day by day,
Or gluttoning on all, or all away.
passages.vernacular: 所以我日復一日憔悴同飽脹,唔係貪食一切,就係一切都離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我日復一日憔悴和飽脹,不是貪食一切,就是一切都離去。

passages.title: Sonnet 76
passages.original:
Why is my verse so barren of new pride,
So far from variation or quick change?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅詩點解咁缺乏新嘅驕傲,咁遠離變化或快速轉變?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的詩為什麼這麼缺乏新的驕傲,這麼遠離變化或快速轉變?

passages.original:
Why with the time do I not glance aside
To new-found methods, and to compounds strange?
passages.vernacular: 點解我唔隨時代轉向新發現嘅方法,同奇異嘅混合物?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼我不隨時代轉向新發現的方法,和奇異的混合物?

passages.original:
Why write I still all one, ever the same,
And keep invention in a noted weed,
That every word doth almost tell my name,
Showing their birth, and where they did proceed?
passages.vernacular: 點解我仍然寫同一樣,永遠相同,將創作保持喺一件著名嘅舊衣中,以致每個字幾乎講出我嘅名,顯示佢哋嘅出身同從何而來?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼我仍然寫同一樣,永遠相同,將創作保持在一件著名的舊衣中,以致每個字幾乎說出我的名,顯示它們的出身和從何而來?

passages.original:
O! know sweet love I always write of you,
And you and love are still my argument;
passages.vernacular: 啊!要知,甜蜜嘅愛,我總係寫你,你同愛仍然係我嘅主題;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!要知,甜蜜的愛,我總是寫你,你和愛仍然是我的主題;

passages.original:
So all my best is dressing old words new,
Spending again what is already spent:
passages.vernacular: 所以我所有最好嘅,就係將舊字換新衣,再花已花過嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我所有最好的,就是將舊字換新衣,再花已花過的:

passages.original:
For as the sun is daily new and old,
So is my love still telling what is told.
passages.vernacular: 因為正如太陽每日新而舊,我嘅愛仍然講著已講過嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為正如太陽每天新而舊,我的愛仍然說著已說過的。

passages.title: Sonnet 77
passages.original:
Thy glass will show thee how thy beauties wear,
Thy dial how thy precious minutes waste;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅鏡子會向你展示你嘅美貌點樣磨損,你嘅日晷點樣令你寶貴嘅分鐘浪費;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的鏡子會向你展示你的美貌怎樣磨損,你的日晷怎樣使你寶貴的分鐘浪費;

passages.original:
These vacant leaves thy mind’s imprint will bear,
And of this book, this learning mayst thou taste.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲空白嘅頁會承載你心靈嘅印記,從這本書,你可以品嚐這個學問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些空白的頁會承載你心靈的印記,從這本書,你可以品嚐這個學問。

passages.original:
The wrinkles which thy glass will truly show
Of mouthed graves will give thee memory;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅鏡子會真實展示嘅皺紋,會畀你張嘴嘅墳墓嘅記憶;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的鏡子會真實展示的皺紋,會給你張嘴的墳墓的記憶;

passages.original:
Thou by thy dial’s shady stealth mayst know
Time’s thievish progress to eternity.
passages.vernacular: 你憑日晷陰影般嘅偷偷摸摸,可以知道時間向永恆嘅竊賊進程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你憑日晷陰影般的偷偷摸摸,可以知道時間向永恆的竊賊進程。

passages.original:
Look! what thy memory cannot contain,
Commit to these waste blanks, and thou shalt find
Those children nursed, deliver’d from thy brain,
To take a new acquaintance of thy mind.
passages.vernacular: 看!你嘅記憶容納唔到嘅,交託畀這些空白,你會發現那些被養育、從你頭腦生出嘅孩子,同你嘅心靈重新認識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看!你的記憶容納不到的,交託給這些空白,你會發現那些被養育、從你頭腦生出的孩子,與你的心靈重新認識。

passages.original:
These offices, so oft as thou wilt look,
Shall profit thee and much enrich thy book.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲職責,只要你願意睇,就會令你得益,並大大豐富你嘅書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些職責,只要你願意看,就會使你得益,並大大豐富你的書。

passages.title: Sonnet 78
passages.original:
So oft have I invoked thee for my Muse,
And found such fair assistance in my verse
As every alien pen hath got my use
And under thee their poesy disperse.
passages.vernacular: 我咁多次祈求你做我嘅繆斯,喺我嘅詩中找到咁美好嘅幫助,以致每枝外來嘅筆都學我嘅用法,在你之下散播佢哋嘅詩篇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這麼多次祈求你做我的繆斯,在我的詩中找到這麼美好的幫助,以致每枝外來的筆都學我的用法,在你之下散播他們的詩篇。

passages.original:
Thine eyes, that taught the dumb on high to sing
And heavy ignorance aloft to fly,
Have added feathers to the learned’s wing
And given grace a double majesty.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅眼睛,教高處嘅啞者歌唱,令沉重嘅無知向上高飛,為博學者嘅翼增添羽毛,畀優雅雙倍嘅威嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的眼睛,教高處的啞者歌唱,使沉重的無知向上高飛,為博學者的翼增添羽毛,給優雅雙倍的威嚴。

passages.original:
Yet be most proud of that which I compile,
Whose influence is thine, and born of thee:
passages.vernacular: 不過最驕傲於我所編嘅,佢嘅影響屬於你,由你而生:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過最驕傲於我所編的,它的影響屬於你,由你而生:

passages.original:
In others’ works thou dost but mend the style,
And arts with thy sweet graces graced be;
passages.vernacular: 在別人嘅作品中,你只係改善文體,藝術因你甜美嘅優雅而增光;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在別人的作品中,你只是改善文體,藝術因你甜美的優雅而增光;

passages.original:
But thou art all my art, and dost advance
As high as learning, my rude ignorance.
passages.vernacular: 不過你係我全部嘅藝術,將我粗魯嘅無知提升到同學問一樣高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你是我全部的藝術,將我粗魯的無知提升到與學問一樣高。

passages.title: Sonnet 79
passages.original:
Whilst I alone did call upon thy aid,
My verse alone had all thy gentle grace;
passages.vernacular: 當只有我呼求你嘅幫助,我嘅詩獨自擁有你全部溫柔嘅優雅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當只有我呼求你的幫助,我的詩獨自擁有你全部溫柔的優雅;

passages.original:
But now my gracious numbers are decay’d,
And my sick Muse doth give an other place.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家我嘅優雅詩句衰敗,我病弱嘅繆斯讓位畀另一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在我的優雅詩句衰敗,我病弱的繆斯讓位給另一個。

passages.original:
I grant, sweet love, thy lovely argument
Deserves the travail of a worthier pen;
passages.vernacular: 我承認,甜蜜嘅愛,你可愛嘅主題值得更有價值嘅筆辛勞;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認,甜蜜的愛,你可愛的主題值得更有價值的筆辛勞;

passages.original:
Yet what of thee thy poet doth invent
He robs thee of, and pays it thee again.
passages.vernacular: 不過你嘅詩人所創作關於你嘅,佢從你身上搶走,再還畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你的詩人所創作關於你的,他從你身上搶走,再還給你。

passages.original:
He lends thee virtue, and he stole that word
From thy behaviour; beauty doth he give,
And found it in thy cheek: he can afford
No praise to thee, but what in thee doth live.
passages.vernacular: 佢借畀你美德,而佢偷咗呢個詞嚟自你嘅行為;佢畀你美貌,卻係在你嘅臉頰上發現:佢畀唔出任何讚美,除咗活喺你身上嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他借給你美德,而他偷了這個詞來自你的行為;他給你美貌,卻是在你的臉頰上發現:他給不出任何讚美,除了活在你身上的。

passages.original:
Then thank him not for that which he doth say,
Since what he owes thee, thou thyself dost pay.
passages.vernacular: 咁唔好因佢所講嘅而感謝佢,因為佢欠你嘅,你自己支付。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那不要因他所說的而感謝他,因為他欠你的,你自己支付。

passages.title: Sonnet 80
passages.original:
O how I faint when I of you do write,
Knowing a better spirit doth use your name,
And in the praise thereof spends all his might,
To make me tongue-tied speaking of your fame!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我寫你嘅時候幾咁暈眩,知道一個更好嘅靈魂使用你嘅名,在對佢嘅讚美中耗盡所有力量,令我談及你嘅名聲時啞口無言!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我寫你的時候多麼暈眩,知道一個更好的靈魂使用你的名,在對它的讚美中耗盡所有力量,使我談及你的名聲時啞口無言!

passages.original:
But since your worth, wide as the ocean is,
The humble as the proudest sail doth bear,
My saucy bark, inferior far to his,
On your broad main doth wilfully appear.
passages.vernacular: 不過既然你嘅價值廣闊如海洋,謙卑嘅帆同最驕傲嘅帆一樣承載,我放肆嘅小船,遠不及佢嘅,任性地出現喺你廣闊嘅海面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過既然你的價值廣闊如海洋,謙卑的帆和最驕傲的帆一樣承載,我放肆的小船,遠不及他的,任性地出現在你廣闊的海面。

passages.original:
Your shallowest help will hold me up afloat,
Whilst he upon your soundless deep doth ride;
passages.vernacular: 你最淺嘅幫助都會托住我浮起,而佢騎喺你深不見底嘅深處;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最淺的幫助都會托住我浮起,而他騎在你深不見底的深處;

passages.original:
Or, being wrack’d, I am a worthless boat,
He of tall building, and of goodly pride:
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果被擊毀,我係一艘冇價值嘅船,佢係高大建築、美好驕傲嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果被擊毀,我是一艘沒價值的船,他是高大建築、美好驕傲的:

passages.original:
Then if he thrive and I be cast away,
The worst was this: my love was my decay.
passages.vernacular: 那麼如果佢興旺而我被拋棄,最壞嘅就係這個:我嘅愛係我嘅毀滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼如果他興旺而我被拋棄,最壞的就是這個:我的愛是我的毀滅。

passages.title: Sonnet 81
passages.original:
Or I shall live your epitaph to make,
Or you survive when I in earth am rotten;
passages.vernacular: 或者我活住為你寫墓誌銘,或者當我喺泥土中腐爛,你仍然活住;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者我活著為你寫墓誌銘,或者當我在泥土中腐爛,你仍然活著;

passages.original:
From hence your memory death cannot take,
Although in me each part will be forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 從此死亡不能奪走你嘅記憶,雖然在我身上每個部分都會被忘記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從此死亡不能奪走你的記憶,雖然在我身上每個部分都會被忘記。

passages.original:
Your name from hence immortal life shall have,
Though I, once gone, to all the world must die:
passages.vernacular: 你嘅名字從此會有永生,雖然我一旦離去,對全世界必須死亡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的名字從此會有永生,雖然我一旦離去,對全世界必須死亡:

passages.original:
The earth can yield me but a common grave,
When you entombed in men’s eyes shall lie.
passages.vernacular: 大地只能畀我一個普通嘅墳墓,而你會葬在人們嘅眼中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大地只能給我一個普通的墳墓,而你會葬在人們的眼中。

passages.original:
Your monument shall be my gentle verse,
Which eyes not yet created shall o’er-read;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅紀念碑會係我溫柔嘅詩,未被創造嘅眼睛會細讀;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的紀念碑會是我溫柔的詩,未被創造的眼睛會細讀;

passages.original:
And tongues to be, your being shall rehearse,
When all the breathers of this world are dead;
passages.vernacular: 將來嘅舌頭會複述你嘅存在,當呢個世界所有呼吸者都已死亡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將來的舌頭會複述你的存在,當這個世界所有呼吸者都已死亡;

passages.original:
You still shall live, such virtue hath my pen,
Where breath most breathes, even in the mouths of men.
passages.vernacular: 你仍然會活著,我嘅筆有咁嘅力量,活喺呼吸最多嘅地方,甚至喺人們嘅口中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你仍然會活著,我的筆有這樣的力量,活在呼吸最多的地方,甚至在人們的口中。

passages.title: Sonnet 82
passages.original:
I grant thou wert not married to my Muse,
And therefore mayst without attaint o’erlook
The dedicated words which writers use
Of their fair subject, blessing every book.
passages.vernacular: 我承認你冇嫁畀我嘅繆斯,所以可以無損咁忽略作家對佢哋美麗主題使用嘅獻辭,祝福每本書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認你沒嫁給我的繆斯,所以可以無損地忽略作家對他們美麗主題使用的獻辭,祝福每本書。

passages.original:
Thou art as fair in knowledge as in hue,
Finding thy worth a limit past my praise;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅知識同膚色一樣美,發現你嘅價值有個超出我讚美嘅極限;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的知識和膚色一樣美,發現你的價值有個超出我讚美的極限;

passages.original:
And therefore art enforced to seek anew
Some fresher stamp of the time-bettering days.
passages.vernacular: 所以被迫重新尋求某個改進時代嘅日子更新鮮嘅印記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以被迫重新尋求某個改進時代的日子更新鮮的印記。

passages.original:
And do so, love; yet when they have devis’d,
What strained touches rhetoric can lend,
Thou truly fair, wert truly sympathiz’d
In true plain words, by thy true-telling friend;
passages.vernacular: 就咁做吧,愛人;不過當佢哋設計出修辭可以借嘅勉強筆觸,你,真正嘅美,被你說真話嘅朋友用真實樸素嘅話真正同情:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣做吧,愛人;不過當他們設計出修辭可以借的勉強筆觸,你,真正的美,被你說真話的朋友用真實樸素的話真正同情:

passages.original:
And their gross painting might be better us’d
Where cheeks need blood; in thee it is abus’d.
passages.vernacular: 而佢哋粗劣嘅塗畫,可以更好咁用喺臉頰需要血色嘅地方;在你身上,就係濫用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而他們粗劣的塗畫,可以更好地用在臉頰需要血色的地方;在你身上,就是濫用。

passages.title: Sonnet 83
passages.original:
I never saw that you did painting need,
And therefore to your fair no painting set;
passages.vernacular: 我從未見過你需要塗畫,所以唔喺你嘅美上加任何塗畫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未見過你需要塗畫,所以不在你的美上加任何塗畫;

passages.original:
I found, or thought I found, you did exceed
That barren tender of a poet’s debt:
passages.vernacular: 我發現,或者以為我發現,你超越詩人債務嗰種貧乏嘅獻禮:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現,或者以為我發現,你超越詩人債務那種貧乏的獻禮:

passages.original:
And therefore have I slept in your report,
That you yourself, being extant, well might show
How far a modern quill doth come too short,
Speaking of worth, what worth in you doth grow.
passages.vernacular: 所以我喺對你嘅描述中睡著,好令你自己,既然存在,可以好好展示現代嘅筆講述價值時,對你身上生長嘅價值多麼不足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我在對你的描述中睡著,好使你自己,既然存在,可以好好展示現代的筆講述價值時,對你身上生長的價值多麼不足。

passages.original:
This silence for my sin you did impute,
Which shall be most my glory being dumb;
passages.vernacular: 你將呢個沉默歸咎於我嘅罪,而佢會成為我最大嘅榮耀,因為啞口:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你將這個沉默歸咎於我的罪,而它會成為我最大的榮耀,因為啞口:

passages.original:
For I impair not beauty being mute,
When others would give life, and bring a tomb.
passages.vernacular: 因為我沉默不損害美貌,當別人想畀生命,卻帶來一座墳墓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我沉默不損害美貌,當別人想給生命,卻帶來一座墳墓。

passages.original:
There lives more life in one of your fair eyes
Than both your poets can in praise devise.
passages.vernacular: 你一隻美麗嘅眼睛裡活著嘅生命,多過你兩個詩人可以用讚美設計出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一隻美麗的眼睛裡活著的生命,多過你兩個詩人可以用讚美設計出來的。

passages.title: Sonnet 84
passages.original:
Who is it that says most, which can say more,
Than this rich praise: that you alone are you,
In whose confine immured is the store
Which should example where your equal grew.
passages.vernacular: 邊個講得最多,可以講比呢個豐富嘅讚美更多:你獨自就係你,在你嘅界限內圍著儲備,應該示範你嘅同等者從何而生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰說得最多,可以說比這個豐富的讚美更多:你獨自就是你,在你的界限內圍著儲備,應該示範你的同等者從何而生?

passages.original:
Lean penury within that pen doth dwell
That to his subject lends not some small glory;
passages.vernacular: 貧乏嘅窮困居住在那枝筆之內,佢唔畀佢嘅主題一點榮耀:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貧乏的窮困居住在那枝筆之內,它不給它的主題一點榮耀:

passages.original:
But he that writes of you, if he can tell
That you are you, so dignifies his story,
Let him but copy what in you is writ,
Not making worse what nature made so clear,
And such a counterpart shall fame his wit,
Making his style admired every where.
passages.vernacular: 不過寫你嘅人,如果佢能夠講你就係你,就令佢嘅故事咁尊貴,只要佢抄寫在你身上寫嘅,唔令大自然造得咁清晰嘅更壞,咁樣嘅對應就會令佢嘅才智出名,令佢嘅文體到處被欣賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過寫你的人,如果他能夠說你就是你,就使他的故事這麼尊貴,只要他抄寫在你身上寫的,不使大自然造得這麼清晰的更壞,這樣的對應就會使他的才智出名,使他的文體到處被欣賞。

passages.original:
You to your beauteous blessings add a curse,
Being fond on praise, which makes your praises worse.
passages.vernacular: 你為你美麗嘅福氣增添一個詛咒,迷戀讚美,令你嘅讚美變得更壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為你美麗的福氣增添一個詛咒,迷戀讚美,使你的讚美變得更壞。

passages.title: Sonnet 85
passages.original:
My tongue-tied Muse in manners holds her still,
While comments of your praise richly compil’d,
Reserve their character with golden quill,
And precious phrase by all the Muses fil’d.
passages.vernacular: 我啞口嘅繆斯出於禮貌保持沉默,而對你讚美嘅評論豐富編纂,用金筆保存佢哋嘅文字,同所有繆斯磨光嘅珍貴措辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我啞口的繆斯出於禮貌保持沉默,而對你讚美的評論豐富編纂,用金筆保存它們的文字,和所有繆斯磨光的珍貴措辭。

passages.original:
I think good thoughts, whilst others write good words,
And like unlettered clerk still cry ‘Amen’
To every hymn that able spirit affords,
In polish’d form of well-refined pen.
passages.vernacular: 我想好嘅念頭,而別人寫好嘅話,好似不識字嘅文書,對有能力嘅靈魂在精煉筆嘅打磨形式中提供嘅每首聖詩,仍然喊「阿們」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想好的念頭,而別人寫好的話,好像不識字的文書,對有能力的靈魂在精煉筆的打磨形式中提供的每首聖詩,仍然喊「阿們」。

passages.original:
Hearing you praised, I say ‘’tis so, ’tis true,’
And to the most of praise add something more;
passages.vernacular: 聽到你被讚美,我講「係,係真」,並喺最大嘅讚美上添加更多:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到你被讚美,我說「是,是真」,並在最大的讚美上添加更多:

passages.original:
But that is in my thought, whose love to you,
Though words come hindmost, holds his rank before.
passages.vernacular: 不過那在我嘅思想中,佢對你嘅愛,雖然言辭最後到,卻保持佢在前嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過那在我的思想中,他對你的愛,雖然言辭最後到,卻保持他在前的位置。

passages.original:
Then others, for the breath of words respect,
Me for my dumb thoughts, speaking in effect.
passages.vernacular: 咁別人因言辭嘅氣息而被尊重,我因我啞口嘅思想,實際上在講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那別人因言辭的氣息而被尊重,我因我啞口的思想,實際上在說話。

passages.title: Sonnet 86
passages.original:
Was it the proud full sail of his great verse,
Bound for the prize of all too precious you,
That did my ripe thoughts in my brain inhearse,
Making their tomb the womb wherein they grew?
passages.vernacular: 係咪佢偉大詩篇驕傲飽滿嘅帆,駛向過分珍貴嘅你嘅獎品,令我頭腦中成熟嘅思想入殮,以佢哋生長嘅子宮作墳墓?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是不是他偉大詩篇驕傲飽滿的帆,駛向過分珍貴的你的獎品,使我頭腦中成熟的思想入殮,以它們生長的子宮作墳墓?

passages.original:
Was it his spirit, by spirits taught to write,
Above a mortal pitch, that struck me dead?
passages.vernacular: 係咪佢嘅靈魂,由靈魂教佢寫作,高於凡人嘅音調,將我擊斃?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是不是他的靈魂,由靈魂教他寫作,高於凡人的音調,將我擊斃?

passages.original:
No, neither he, nor his compeers by night
Giving him aid, my verse astonished.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢唔係,夜晚幫佢嘅同伴亦唔係,令我嘅詩震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他不是,夜晚幫他的同伴也不是,使我的詩震驚。

passages.vernacular: 佢,同嗰個每晚用情報愚弄佢嘅和藹熟悉嘅鬼,都唔能夠作為我沉默嘅勝利者誇口;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他,和那個每晚用情報愚弄他的和藹熟悉的鬼,都不能夠作為我沉默的勝利者誇口;

passages.original: I was not sick of any fear from thence:
passages.vernacular: 我並唔因此而感到任何恐懼:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我並不因此而感到任何恐懼:

passages.original:
But when your countenance fill’d up his line,
Then lacked I matter; that enfeebled mine.
passages.vernacular: 不過當你嘅容顏填滿佢嘅詩行,我就欠缺題材;呢個令我嘅衰弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當你的容顏填滿他的詩行,我就欠缺題材;這使我的衰弱。

passages.title: Sonnet 87
passages.vernacular: 再見!你太珍貴,我不能擁有,你很可能知道你嘅估價,你價值嘅特許狀賦予你解約權;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見!你太珍貴,我不能擁有,你很可能知道你的估價,你價值的特許狀賦予你解約權;

passages.original: My bonds in thee are all determinate.
passages.vernacular: 我對你嘅一切契約都已終止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對你的一切契約都已終止。

passages.original: For how do I hold thee but by thy granting?
passages.vernacular: 因為除咗你嘅恩賜,我點樣擁有你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為除了你的恩賜,我怎樣擁有你?

passages.original: And for that riches where is my deserving?
passages.vernacular: 而對於呢種財富,我有咩功績?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而對於這種財富,我有什麼功績?

passages.original:
The cause of this fair gift in me is wanting,
And so my patent back again is swerving.
passages.vernacular: 我身上欠缺呢份美好禮物嘅理由,所以我嘅專利又偏離回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我身上欠缺這份美好禮物的理由,所以我的專利又偏離回去。

passages.original:
Thyself thou gav’st, thy own worth then not knowing,
Or me to whom thou gav’st it, else mistaking;
passages.vernacular: 你畀咗你自己,當時不知道你自己嘅價值,或者錯看我,你畀嘅對象;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你給了你自己,當時不知道你自己的價值,或者錯看我,你給的對象;

passages.original:
So thy great gift, upon misprision growing,
Comes home again, on better judgement making.
passages.vernacular: 所以你嘅偉大禮物,在誤判上生長,憑更好嘅判斷歸還。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你的偉大禮物,在誤判上生長,憑更好的判斷歸還。

passages.original:
Thus have I had thee, as a dream doth flatter,
In sleep a king, but waking no such matter.
passages.vernacular: 就咁我擁有過你,好似夢奉承,睡中做國王,醒來卻冇咁回事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣我擁有過你,好像夢奉承,睡中做國王,醒來卻沒這回事。

passages.title: Sonnet 88
passages.original:
When thou shalt be dispos’d to set me light,
And place my merit in the eye of scorn,
Upon thy side, against myself I’ll fight,
And prove thee virtuous, though thou art forsworn.
passages.vernacular: 當你傾向看輕我,將我嘅功績放在輕蔑嘅眼中,我會站在你一邊,同我自己作戰,證明你有德,雖然你背棄誓言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你傾向看輕我,將我的功績放在輕蔑的眼中,我會站在你一邊,與我自己作戰,證明你有德,雖然你背棄誓言。

passages.vernacular: 最熟悉我自己嘅軟弱,我可以為你嗰邊寫下一個隱藏過失嘅故事,其中我被判有罪;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最熟悉我自己的軟弱,我可以為你那邊寫下一個隱藏過失的故事,其中我被判有罪;

passages.original: That thou in losing me shalt win much glory:
passages.vernacular: 令你失去我而贏得好多榮耀:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使你失去我而贏得很多榮耀:

passages.original: And I by this will be a gainer too;
passages.vernacular: 而我藉此亦會成為得益者;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我藉此也會成為得益者;

passages.original:
For bending all my loving thoughts on thee,
The injuries that to myself I do,
Doing thee vantage, double-vantage me.
passages.vernacular: 因為將我所有愛嘅思想傾向你,我對自己所做嘅傷害,令你得益,令我雙倍得益。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為將我所有愛的思想傾向你,我對自己所做的傷害,使你得益,使我雙倍得益。

passages.original:
Such is my love, to thee I so belong,
That for thy right, myself will bear all wrong.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅愛就係咁,我如此屬於你,為咗你嘅權利,我自己會承受所有錯待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的愛就是這樣,我如此屬於你,為了你的權利,我自己會承受所有錯待。

passages.title: Sonnet 89
passages.original:
Say that thou didst forsake me for some fault,
And I will comment upon that offence:
passages.vernacular: 話你因為某個過失拋棄我,我就會評論嗰個冒犯:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說你因為某個過失拋棄我,我就會評論那個冒犯:

passages.original:
Speak of my lameness, and I straight will halt,
Against thy reasons making no defence.
passages.vernacular: 講我跛,我即刻就一拐一拐,對你嘅理由唔作任何辯護。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說我跛,我立刻就一拐一拐,對你的理由不作任何辯護。

passages.original:
Thou canst not love disgrace me half so ill,
To set a form upon desired change,
As I’ll myself disgrace; knowing thy will,
I will acquaintance strangle, and look strange;
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠用愛令我蒙羞,為想要嘅改變定下形式,有我自己令自己蒙羞咁差;知道你嘅意願,我會扼殺相識,看來陌生;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能夠用愛使我蒙羞,為想要的改變定下形式,有我自己使自己蒙羞那麼差;知道你的意願,我會扼殺相識,看來陌生;

passages.original:
Be absent from thy walks; and in my tongue
Thy sweet beloved name no more shall dwell,
Lest I, too much profane, should do it wrong,
And haply of our old acquaintance tell.
passages.vernacular: 唔出現在你散步嘅地方;我嘅舌頭上你甜美親愛嘅名字再唔居住,免得我太褻瀆,弄錯了它,偶然講起我哋舊日嘅相識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不出現在你散步的地方;我的舌頭上你甜美親愛的名字再不居住,免得我太褻瀆,弄錯了它,偶然說起我們舊日的相識。

passages.original:
For thee, against my self I’ll vow debate,
For I must ne’er love him whom thou dost hate.
passages.vernacular: 為咗你,我會對自己發誓爭辯,因為我永遠不能愛你所恨嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了你,我會對自己發誓爭辯,因為我永遠不能愛你所恨的人。

passages.title: Sonnet 90
passages.original: Then hate me when thou wilt; if ever, now;
passages.vernacular: 咁你想恨我就恨我吧;如果有一次,就而家:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你想恨我就恨我吧;如果有一次,就現在:

passages.original:
Now, while the world is bent my deeds to cross,
Join with the spite of fortune, make me bow,
And do not drop in for an after-loss:
passages.vernacular: 而家,當世界傾向阻撓我嘅行為,同命運嘅怨恨聯手,令我低頭,唔好之後再加一重損失:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,當世界傾向阻撓我的行為,與命運的怨恨聯手,使我低頭,不要之後再加一重損失:

passages.original:
Ah! do not, when my heart hath ’scap’d this sorrow,
Come in the rearward of a conquer’d woe;
passages.vernacular: 啊!唔好,當我嘅心逃過呢個悲傷,唔好跟在被征服嘅苦難後面進來;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!不要,當我的心逃過這個悲傷,不要跟在被征服的苦難後面進來;

passages.original:
Give not a windy night a rainy morrow,
To linger out a purpos’d overthrow.
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀大風夜一個下雨嘅明朝,拖延一場已定嘅傾覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要給大風夜一個下雨的明朝,拖延一場已定的傾覆。

passages.original:
If thou wilt leave me, do not leave me last,
When other petty griefs have done their spite,
But in the onset come: so shall I taste
At first the very worst of fortune’s might;
passages.vernacular: 如果你要離開我,唔好最後先離開,當其他細小嘅悲傷已經發完佢哋嘅怨恨,而係一開始就來:咁我一開始就嚐到命運力量最壞嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你要離開我,不要最後才離開,當其他細小的悲傷已經發完它們的怨恨,而是一開始就來:這樣我一開始就嘗到命運力量最壞的;

passages.original:
And other strains of woe, which now seem woe,
Compar’d with loss of thee, will not seem so.
passages.vernacular: 而其他悲痛嘅曲調,而家似乎係悲痛,同失去你比較,就唔會咁似。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而其他悲痛的曲調,現在似乎是悲痛,與失去你比較,就不會這樣似。

passages.title: Sonnet 91
passages.vernacular: 有些人以出身為榮,有些以技藝,有些以財富,有些以身體嘅力量,有些以佢哋嘅衣服(雖然式樣新奇而壞);
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人以出身為榮,有些以技藝,有些以財富,有些以身體的力量,有些以他們的衣服(雖然式樣新奇而壞);

passages.original: Some in their hawks and hounds, some in their horse;
passages.vernacular: 有些以佢哋嘅鷹同獵犬,有些以佢哋嘅馬;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些以他們的鷹和獵犬,有些以他們的馬;

passages.original:
And every humour hath his adjunct pleasure,
Wherein it finds a joy above the rest:
passages.vernacular: 每種性情都有佢附帶嘅樂趣,在其中找到高於其餘嘅喜悅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每種性情都有它附帶的樂趣,在其中找到高於其餘的喜悅:

passages.original:
But these particulars are not my measure,
All these I better in one general best.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢啲細節唔係我嘅衡量標準,所有這些我都用一個總的最好去勝過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這些細節不是我的衡量標準,所有這些我都用一個總的最好去勝過。

passages.vernacular: 你嘅愛對我嚟講比高貴出身更好,比財富更富有,比衣服價錢更驕傲,比鷹同馬更令人歡喜;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的愛對我來說比高貴出身更好,比財富更富有,比衣服價錢更驕傲,比鷹和馬更令人歡喜;

passages.original: And having thee, of all men’s pride I boast:
passages.vernacular: 有咗你,我就誇耀所有人嘅驕傲:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有了你,我就誇耀所有人的驕傲:

passages.original:
Wretched in this alone, that thou mayst take
All this away, and me most wretched make.
passages.vernacular: 只有一點悲慘,就係你可能將所有呢啲拿走,令我最悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有一點悲慘,就是你可能將所有這些拿走,使我最悲慘。

passages.title: Sonnet 92
passages.original:
But do thy worst to steal thyself away,
For term of life thou art assured mine;
passages.vernacular: 不過盡你最壞嘅偷走你自己吧,你一生都肯定屬於我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過盡你最壞的偷走你自己吧,你一生都肯定屬於我;

passages.original:
And life no longer than thy love will stay,
For it depends upon that love of thine.
passages.vernacular: 而生命只維持到你嘅愛停留嘅時間,因為佢依賴你嗰份愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而生命只維持到你的愛停留的時間,因為它依賴你那份愛。

passages.original:
Then need I not to fear the worst of wrongs,
When in the least of them my life hath end.
passages.vernacular: 咁我唔需要怕最壞嘅錯待,因為在最輕微嘅一個中,我嘅生命就終結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我不需要怕最壞的錯待,因為在最輕微的一個中,我的生命就終結。

passages.original:
I see a better state to me belongs
Than that which on thy humour doth depend:
passages.vernacular: 我見到有一個更好嘅狀態屬於我,勝過依賴你性情嘅那個:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看到有一個更好的狀態屬於我,勝過依賴你性情的那個:

passages.original:
Thou canst not vex me with inconstant mind,
Since that my life on thy revolt doth lie.
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠用善變嘅心惹惱我,因為我嘅生命在你嘅背叛上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能夠用善變的心惹惱我,因為我的生命在你的背叛上。

passages.original:
O! what a happy title do I find,
Happy to have thy love, happy to die!
passages.vernacular: 啊!我找到幾幸福嘅名分,有你嘅愛就快樂,死亦快樂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!我找到多幸福的名分,有你的愛就快樂,死也快樂!

passages.original: But what’s so blessed-fair that fears no blot?
passages.vernacular: 不過有咩係有福嘅美,卻唔怕污點?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過有什麼是有福的美,卻不怕污點?

passages.original: Thou mayst be false, and yet I know it not.
passages.vernacular: 你可能虛假,而我卻唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可能虛假,而我卻不知道。

passages.title: Sonnet 93
passages.vernacular: 所以我活下去,假設你真誠,好似被欺騙嘅丈夫;所以愛嘅臉在我看來仍可能是愛,雖然已改變:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我活下去,假設你真誠,好像被欺騙的丈夫;所以愛的臉在我看來仍可能是愛,雖然已改變:

passages.original: Thy looks with me, thy heart in other place:
passages.vernacular: 你嘅神情同我在一起,你嘅心在別處:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的神情與我在一起,你的心在別處:

passages.original:
For there can live no hatred in thine eye,
Therefore in that I cannot know thy change.
passages.vernacular: 因為你嘅眼中不能存在恨,所以憑那個我知道不到你嘅改變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你的眼中不能存在恨,所以憑那個我知道不到你的改變。

passages.original:
In many’s looks, the false heart’s history
Is writ in moods, and frowns, and wrinkles strange.
passages.vernacular: 在許多人嘅神情中,虛假之心嘅歷史,寫喺情緒、皺眉同奇怪嘅皺紋裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在許多人的神情中,虛假之心的歷史,寫在情緒、皺眉和奇怪的皺紋裡。

passages.original:
But heaven in thy creation did decree
That in thy face sweet love should ever dwell;
passages.vernacular: 不過天在造你時決定,在你嘅臉上甜蜜嘅愛應該永遠居住;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過天在造你時決定,在你的臉上甜蜜的愛應該永遠居住;

passages.original:
Whate’er thy thoughts, or thy heart’s workings be,
Thy looks should nothing thence, but sweetness tell.
passages.vernacular: 無論你嘅思想,或你心嘅運作係咩,你嘅神情從那裡不應該講任何東西,只有甜蜜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論你的思想,或你心的運作是什麼,你的神情從那裡不應該說任何東西,只有甜蜜。

passages.original:
How like Eve’s apple doth thy beauty grow,
If thy sweet virtue answer not thy show!
passages.vernacular: 你嘅美貌長得幾似夏娃嘅蘋果,如果你甜美嘅美德唔回應你嘅外表!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的美貌長得多像夏娃的蘋果,如果你甜美的美德不回應你的外表!

passages.title: Sonnet 94
passages.original:
They that have power to hurt, and will do none,
That do not do the thing they most do show,
Who, moving others, are themselves as stone,
Unmoved, cold, and to temptation slow;
passages.vernacular: 有力量傷害卻唔傷害,唔做佢哋最表現出嚟要做嘅事,感動別人而自己如石頭,不動、冷漠、對誘惑遲緩嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有力量傷害卻不傷害,不做他們最表現出來要做的事,感動別人而自己如石頭,不動、冷漠、對誘惑遲緩的人;

passages.original:
They rightly do inherit heaven’s graces,
And husband nature’s riches from expense;
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正當地繼承天嘅恩典,並保護大自然嘅財富免於花費;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們正當地繼承天的恩典,並保護大自然的財富免於花費;

passages.original:
They are the lords and owners of their faces,
Others, but stewards of their excellence.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係自己臉孔嘅主人同擁有者,其他人只不過係佢哋卓越嘅管家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們是自己臉孔的主人和擁有者,其他人只不過是他們卓越的管家。

passages.original:
The summer’s flower is to the summer sweet,
Though to itself, it only live and die,
But if that flower with base infection meet,
The basest weed outbraves his dignity:
passages.vernacular: 夏天嘅花對夏天來講係甜美,雖然對自己,佢只係生同死,不過如果那朵花遇上卑劣嘅感染,最卑賤嘅雜草都勝過佢嘅尊嚴:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏天的花對夏天來說是甜美,雖然對自己,它只是生和死,不過如果那朵花遇上卑劣的感染,最卑賤的雜草都勝過它的尊嚴:

passages.original: For sweetest things turn sourest by their deeds;
passages.vernacular: 因為最甜美嘅事物憑佢哋嘅行為變成最酸苦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為最甜美的事物憑它們的行為變成最酸苦;

passages.original: Lilies that fester, smell far worse than weeds.
passages.vernacular: 潰爛嘅百合,比雜草臭得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潰爛的百合,比雜草臭得多。

passages.title: Sonnet 95
passages.original:
How sweet and lovely dost thou make the shame
Which, like a canker in the fragrant rose,
Doth spot the beauty of thy budding name!
passages.vernacular: 你將羞恥變得幾甜美可愛,佢好似芬芳玫瑰中嘅蛀蟲,玷污你萌芽名字嘅美!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你將羞恥變得多甜美可愛,它好像芬芳玫瑰中的蛀蟲,玷污你萌芽名字的美!

passages.original: O! in what sweets dost thou thy sins enclose.
passages.vernacular: 啊!你將你嘅罪封喺幾甜蜜嘅東西裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!你將你的罪封在多甜蜜的東西裡。

passages.vernacular: 講述你日子故事嘅舌頭,對你嘅嬉戲作放蕩嘅評論,不能貶低,只能用一種讚美:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講述你日子故事的舌頭,對你的嬉戲作放蕩的評論,不能貶低,只能用一種讚美:

passages.original: Naming thy name, blesses an ill report.
passages.vernacular: 叫你嘅名字,祝福一個壞名聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫你的名字,祝福一個壞名聲。

passages.original:
O! what a mansion have those vices got
Which for their habitation chose out thee,
Where beauty’s veil doth cover every blot
And all things turns to fair that eyes can see!
passages.vernacular: 啊!那些惡習得到幾好嘅一座大宅,選咗你做佢哋嘅居所,在嗰度美貌嘅面紗遮住每個污點,將眼睛所見嘅一切都變成美好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!那些惡習得到多好的一座大宅,選了你做它們的居所,在那裡美貌的面紗遮住每個污點,將眼睛所見的一切都變成美好!

passages.original: Take heed, dear heart, of this large privilege;
passages.vernacular: 小心,親愛嘅心,呢個巨大嘅特權;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小心,親愛的心,這個巨大的特權;

passages.original: The hardest knife ill-us’d doth lose his edge.
passages.vernacular: 最硬嘅刀用得不好,都會失去鋒刃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最硬的刀用得不好,也會失去鋒刃。

passages.title: Sonnet 96
passages.original: Some say thy fault is youth, some wantonness;
passages.vernacular: 有些人話你嘅過失係年輕,有些話係放蕩;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人說你的過失是年輕,有些說是放蕩;

passages.original: Some say thy grace is youth and gentle sport;
passages.vernacular: 有些人話你嘅優雅係年輕同溫柔嘅嬉戲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人說你的優雅是年輕和溫柔的嬉戲;

passages.original: Both grace and faults are lov’d of more and less:
passages.vernacular: 優雅同過失都被或多或少嘅人所愛:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 優雅和過失都被或多或少的人所愛:

passages.original: Thou mak’st faults graces that to thee resort.
passages.vernacular: 你令求助於你嘅過失變成優雅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你使求助於你的過失變成優雅。

passages.original:
As on the finger of a throned queen
The basest jewel will be well esteem’d,
So are those errors that in thee are seen
To truths translated, and for true things deem’d.
passages.vernacular: 好似在登基女王嘅手指上,最卑賤嘅珠寶都會被好好珍視,在你身上見到嘅那些錯誤也一樣,被轉化成真,被當作真嘅事物:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像在登基女王的手指上,最卑賤的珠寶都會被好好珍視,在你身上看到的那些錯誤也一樣,被轉化成真,被當作真的事物:

passages.original:
How many lambs might the stern wolf betray,
If like a lamb he could his looks translate!
passages.vernacular: 如果嚴厲嘅狼可以將佢嘅神情轉化成羔羊,佢會出賣幾多羊羔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果嚴厲的狼可以將他的神情轉化成羔羊,他會出賣多少羊羔!

passages.original:
How many gazers mightst thou lead away,
If thou wouldst use the strength of all thy state!
passages.vernacular: 如果你運用你所有地位嘅力量,你會帶走幾多凝望者!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你運用你所有地位的力量,你會帶走多少凝望者!

passages.original:
But do not so; I love thee in such sort,
As, thou being mine, mine is thy good report.
passages.vernacular: 不過唔好咁做;我愛你到如此程度,以致你屬於我,你嘅好名聲就屬於我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過不要這樣做;我愛你到如此程度,以致你屬於我,你的好名聲就屬於我。

passages.title: Sonnet 97
passages.original:
How like a winter hath my absence been
From thee, the pleasure of the fleeting year!
passages.vernacular: 我離開你嘅缺席,多似一個冬天,你係流逝一年嘅歡愉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我離開你的缺席,多像一個冬天,你是流逝一年的歡愉!

passages.original: What freezings have I felt, what dark days seen!
passages.vernacular: 我感受過幾多冰凍,見過幾多黑暗嘅日子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感受過多少冰凍,看過多少黑暗的日子!

passages.original: What old December’s bareness everywhere!
passages.vernacular: 到處係舊十二月嘅光禿!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到處是舊十二月的光禿!

passages.original: And yet this time removed was summer’s time;
passages.vernacular: 然而呢段被移走嘅時間係夏天嘅時間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而這段被移走的時間是夏天的時間;

passages.original:
The teeming autumn, big with rich increase,
Bearing the wanton burden of the prime,
Like widow’d wombs after their lords’ decease:
passages.vernacular: 多產嘅秋天,懷著豐富嘅收成,承載盛年嘅放縱重擔,好似丈夫去世後嘅寡婦子宮:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多產的秋天,懷著豐富的收成,承載盛年的放縱重擔,好像丈夫去世後的寡婦子宮:

passages.original:
Yet this abundant issue seem’d to me
But hope of orphans, and unfather’d fruit;
passages.vernacular: 然而這些豐富嘅後代對我來講只似孤兒嘅希望,無父嘅果實;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而這些豐富的後代對我來說只像孤兒的希望,無父的果實;

passages.original:
For summer and his pleasures wait on thee,
And, thou away, the very birds are mute:
passages.vernacular: 因為夏天同佢嘅歡愉侍奉你,你不在,連鳥都啞了:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為夏天和他的歡愉侍奉你,你不在,連鳥都啞了:

passages.original:
Or, if they sing, ’tis with so dull a cheer,
That leaves look pale, dreading the winter’s near.
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果佢哋唱,都帶住咁遲鈍嘅神情,令葉子蒼白,害怕冬天臨近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果它們唱,都帶著這麼遲鈍的神情,使葉子蒼白,害怕冬天臨近。

passages.title: Sonnet 98
passages.original:
From you have I been absent in the spring,
When proud-pied April, dress’d in all his trim,
Hath put a spirit of youth in every thing,
That heavy Saturn laugh’d and leap’d with him.
passages.vernacular: 春天我離開咗你,當驕傲斑斕嘅四月穿上所有佢嘅裝飾,在每樣事物中放入青春嘅精神,令沉重嘅土星都同佢一齊笑同跳;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 春天我離開了你,當驕傲斑斕的四月穿上所有他的裝飾,在每樣事物中放入青春的精神,使沉重的土星都與他一起笑和跳;

passages.original:
Yet nor the lays of birds, nor the sweet smell
Of different flowers in odour and in hue,
Could make me any summer’s story tell,
Or from their proud lap pluck them where they grew:
passages.vernacular: 然而無論鳥嘅歌,還是不同香氣同顏色嘅花嘅甜美氣味,都不能令我講任何夏天嘅故事,或從佢哋驕傲嘅膝上,在佢哋生長處摘取佢哋:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而無論鳥的歌,還是不同香氣和顏色的花的甜美氣味,都不能使我說任何夏天的故事,或從它們驕傲的膝上,在它們生長處摘取它們:

passages.original:
Nor did I wonder at the lily’s white,
Nor praise the deep vermilion in the rose;
passages.vernacular: 我亦唔驚嘆百合嘅白,亦唔讚美玫瑰深紅嘅硃紅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不驚嘆百合的白,也不讚美玫瑰深紅的硃紅;

passages.original:
They were but sweet, but figures of delight,
Drawn after you, you pattern of all those.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋只不過係甜,只不過係歡愉嘅形象,照你描繪,你係所有呢啲嘅範本。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們只不過是甜,只不過是歡愉的形象,照你描繪,你是所有這些的範本。

passages.original:
Yet seem’d it winter still, and you away,
As with your shadow I with these did play.
passages.vernacular: 然而仍然似冬天,你不在,好似我同呢啲同你嘅影子玩耍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而仍然像冬天,你不在,好像我與這些和你的影子玩耍。

passages.title: Sonnet 99
passages.original: The forward violet thus did I chide:
passages.vernacular: 我咁樣責備早開嘅紫羅蘭:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這樣責備早開的紫羅蘭:

passages.original:
Sweet thief, whence didst thou steal thy sweet that smells,
If not from my love’s breath? The purple pride
Which on thy soft cheek for complexion dwells
In my love’s veins thou hast too grossly dy’d.
passages.vernacular: 甜蜜嘅賊,你從邊度偷走你嘅香氣,如果唔係從我愛人嘅氣息?你柔軟臉頰上嘅紫色驕傲,作為膚色,你太粗糙咁染在我愛人嘅血管裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甜蜜的賊,你從哪裡偷走你的香氣,如果不是從我愛人的氣息?你柔軟臉頰上的紫色驕傲,作為膚色,你太粗糙地染在我愛人的血管裡。

passages.original:
The lily I condemned for thy hand,
And buds of marjoram had stol’n thy hair;
passages.vernacular: 百合我因你嘅手而譴責,而墨角蘭嘅花蕾偷走咗你嘅頭髮;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 百合我因你的手而譴責,而墨角蘭的花蕾偷走了你的頭髮;

passages.original:
The roses fearfully on thorns did stand,
One blushing shame, another white despair;
passages.vernacular: 玫瑰恐懼地站喺刺上,一朵臉紅羞愧,另一朵白色絕望;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玫瑰恐懼地站在刺上,一朵臉紅羞愧,另一朵白色絕望;

passages.original:
A third, nor red nor white, had stol’n of both,
And to his robbery had annex’d thy breath;
passages.vernacular: 第三朵,既唔紅亦唔白,兩者都偷咗,並將你嘅氣息附加在佢嘅搶劫上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第三朵,既不紅也不白,兩者都偷了,並將你的氣息附加在他的搶劫上;

passages.original:
But, for his theft, in pride of all his growth
A vengeful canker eat him up to death.
passages.vernacular: 不過因為佢嘅盜竊,在佢全部生長嘅驕傲中,一條報復嘅蛀蟲將佢吃到死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過因為他的盜竊,在他全部生長的驕傲中,一條報復的蛀蟲將他吃到死。

passages.original:
More flowers I noted, yet I none could see,
But sweet, or colour it had stol’n from thee.
passages.vernacular: 我留意到更多花,卻見唔到任何一朵,唔係從你偷嚟甜香或顏色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我留意到更多花,卻看不到任何一朵,不是從你偷來甜香或顏色。

passages.title: Sonnet 100
passages.original:
Where art thou Muse that thou forget’st so long,
To speak of that which gives thee all thy might?
passages.vernacular: 繆斯,你喺邊,咁耐都忘記講賦予你全部力量嘅人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繆斯,你在哪,這麼久都忘記說賦予你全部力量的人?

passages.original:
Spend’st thou thy fury on some worthless song,
Darkening thy power to lend base subjects light?
passages.vernacular: 你係咪將你嘅狂熱花喺某首冇價值嘅歌上,遮暗你嘅力量去為卑賤嘅主題借光?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是不是將你的狂熱花在某首沒價值的歌上,遮暗你的力量去為卑賤的主題借光?

passages.original:
Return forgetful Muse, and straight redeem,
In gentle numbers time so idly spent;
passages.vernacular: 返嚟啦,健忘嘅繆斯,即刻用溫柔嘅詩句贖回咁閒散花掉嘅時間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回來吧,健忘的繆斯,立刻用溫柔的詩句贖回這麼閒散花掉的時間;

passages.original:
Sing to the ear that doth thy lays esteem
And gives thy pen both skill and argument.
passages.vernacular: 唱畀欣賞你詩歌嘅耳朵聽,佢畀你嘅筆技巧同主題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱給欣賞你詩歌的耳朵聽,他給你的筆技巧和主題。

passages.original:
Rise, resty Muse, my love’s sweet face survey,
If Time have any wrinkle graven there;
passages.vernacular: 起身啦,懶惰嘅繆斯,審視我愛人甜美嘅臉,睇下時間有冇喺嗰度刻下任何皺紋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起身吧,懶惰的繆斯,審視我愛人甜美的臉,看看時間有沒有在那裡刻下任何皺紋;

passages.original:
If any, be a satire to decay,
And make time’s spoils despised every where.
passages.vernacular: 如果有,就對衰敗作諷刺,令時間嘅掠奪到處被鄙視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有,就對衰敗作諷刺,使時間的掠奪到處被鄙視。

passages.original:
Give my love fame faster than Time wastes life,
So thou prevent’st his scythe and crooked knife.
passages.vernacular: 畀我愛人名聲,快過時間浪費生命,咁你就阻止佢嘅鐮刀同彎刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我愛人名聲,快過時間浪費生命,這樣你就阻止他的鐮刀和彎刀。

passages.title: Sonnet 101
passages.original:
O truant Muse what shall be thy amends
For thy neglect of truth in beauty dy’d?
passages.vernacular: 啊逃學嘅繆斯,你會點樣補償你對染上美嘅真嘅忽視?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊逃學的繆斯,你會怎樣補償你對染上美的真的忽視?

passages.original: Both truth and beauty on my love depends;
passages.vernacular: 真同美都依賴我嘅愛人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真和美都依賴我的愛人;

passages.original: So dost thou too, and therein dignified.
passages.vernacular: 你都一樣,並因此得到尊貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也一樣,並因此得到尊貴。

passages.original:
Make answer Muse: wilt thou not haply say,
‘Truth needs no colour, with his colour fix’d;
passages.vernacular: 回答啦繆斯:你會唔會偶然講:「真唔需要顏色,佢嘅顏色已固定;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回答吧繆斯:你會不會偶然說:「真不需要顏色,他的顏色已固定;

passages.original: Beauty no pencil, beauty’s truth to lay;
passages.vernacular: 美唔需要畫筆來鋪陳美嘅真;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美不需要畫筆來鋪陳美的真;

passages.original: But best is best, if never intermix’d’?
passages.vernacular: 不過最好就係最好,如果從不混合」?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過最好就是最好,如果從不混合」?

passages.original: Because he needs no praise, wilt thou be dumb?
passages.vernacular: 因為佢唔需要讚美,你就要啞口?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他不需要讚美,你就要啞口?

passages.original:
Excuse not silence so, for’t lies in thee
To make him much outlive a gilded tomb
And to be prais’d of ages yet to be.
passages.vernacular: 唔好咁樣為沉默辯解,因為你可以令佢比鍍金嘅墳墓活得久得多,並被未來嘅年代讚美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要這樣為沉默辯解,因為你可以使他比鍍金的墳墓活得久得多,並被未來的年代讚美。

passages.original:
Then do thy office, Muse; I teach thee how
To make him seem long hence as he shows now.
passages.vernacular: 咁做你嘅職責啦,繆斯;我教你點樣令佢在好耐之後顯得似而家咁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那做你的職責吧,繆斯;我教你怎樣使他在很久之後顯得像現在這樣。

passages.title: Sonnet 102
passages.original: My love is strengthen’d, though more weak in seeming;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅愛加強咗,雖然看起來更弱;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的愛加強了,雖然看起來更弱;

passages.original: I love not less, though less the show appear;
passages.vernacular: 我並唔少愛,雖然外表少咗;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我並不少愛,雖然外表少了;

passages.original:
That love is merchandiz’d, whose rich esteeming,
The owner’s tongue doth publish every where.
passages.vernacular: 被當作商品嘅愛,係擁有者嘅舌頭到處宣揚佢豐富嘅估價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被當作商品的愛,是擁有者的舌頭到處宣揚它豐富的估價。

passages.original:
Our love was new, and then but in the spring,
When I was wont to greet it with my lays;
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅愛係新嘅,當時只在春天,我慣於用我嘅詩歌問候它;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的愛是新的,當時只在春天,我慣於用我的詩歌問候它;

passages.original:
As Philomel in summer’s front doth sing,
And stops her pipe in growth of riper days:
passages.vernacular: 好似夜鶯在夏天嘅前頭歌唱,在較成熟日子嘅生長中停止佢嘅笛:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像夜鶯在夏天的前頭歌唱,在較成熟日子的生長中停止她的笛:

passages.original:
Not that the summer is less pleasant now
Than when her mournful hymns did hush the night,
But that wild music burthens every bough,
And sweets grown common lose their dear delight.
passages.vernacular: 並唔係夏天而家比佢哀傷嘅詩歌令夜晚寂靜時更不愉快,而係狂野嘅音樂壓滿每條枝,變得普通嘅甜美失去佢哋親愛嘅歡愉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並不是夏天現在比她哀傷的詩歌使夜晚寂靜時更不愉快,而是狂野的音樂壓滿每條枝,變得普通的甜美失去它們親愛的歡愉。

passages.original: Therefore like her, I sometime hold my tongue:
passages.vernacular: 所以我像佢一樣,有時收住舌頭:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我像她一樣,有時收住舌頭:

passages.original: Because I would not dull you with my song.
passages.vernacular: 因為我唔想用我嘅歌令你厭倦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我不想用我的歌使你厭倦。

passages.title: Sonnet 103
passages.original:
Alack! what poverty my Muse brings forth,
That having such a scope to show her pride,
The argument, all bare, is of more worth
Than when it hath my added praise beside!
passages.vernacular: 唉!我嘅繆斯帶來咁貧乏,明明有咁大範圍展示佢嘅驕傲,主題完全赤裸,比有我額外讚美時更有價值!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉!我的繆斯帶來這麼貧乏,明明有這麼大範圍展示她的驕傲,主題完全赤裸,比有我額外讚美時更有價值!

passages.original: O! blame me not, if I no more can write!
passages.vernacular: 啊!如果我唔能再寫,唔好怪我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!如果我不能再寫,不要怪我!

passages.original:
Look in your glass, and there appears a face
That over-goes my blunt invention quite,
Dulling my lines, and doing me disgrace.
passages.vernacular: 望落你嘅鏡子,那裡出現一張臉,完全超越我遲鈍嘅創作,令我嘅詩行遲鈍,令我蒙羞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 望向你的鏡子,那裡出現一張臉,完全超越我遲鈍的創作,使我的詩行遲鈍,使我蒙羞。

passages.original:
Were it not sinful then, striving to mend,
To mar the subject that before was well?
passages.vernacular: 咁努力改進,卻破壞原本好好嘅主題,唔係罪過嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那努力改進,卻破壞原本好好的主題,不是罪過嗎?

passages.original:
For to no other pass my verses tend
Than of your graces and your gifts to tell;
passages.vernacular: 因為我嘅詩只不過傾向講述你嘅優雅同你嘅天賦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我的詩只不過傾向講述你的優雅和你的天賦;

passages.original:
And more, much more, than in my verse can sit,
Your own glass shows you when you look in it.
passages.vernacular: 而更多,多得多,比我嘅詩可以容納嘅,你自己嘅鏡子在你望入去時展示畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而更多,多得多,比我的詩可以容納的,你自己的鏡子在你望進去時展示給你。

passages.title: Sonnet 104
passages.original:
To me, fair friend, you never can be old,
For as you were when first your eye I ey’d,
Such seems your beauty still. Three winters cold,
Have from the forests shook three summers’ pride,
Three beauteous springs to yellow autumn turn’d,
In process of the seasons have I seen,
Three April perfumes in three hot Junes burn’d,
Since first I saw you fresh, which yet are green.
passages.vernacular: 對我嚟講,美麗嘅朋友,你永遠唔會老,因為你同我第一次望住你眼睛時一樣,你嘅美貌看來仍然咁。三個寒冷嘅冬天,已從森林搖落三個夏天嘅驕傲,三個美麗嘅春天隨季節嘅過程變成黃色嘅秋天,三個四月嘅香氣在三個炎熱嘅六月燃燒,自從我第一次見到你清新,而你仍然青翠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說,美麗的朋友,你永遠不會老,因為你與我第一次望著你眼睛時一樣,你的美貌看來仍然這樣。三個寒冷的冬天,已從森林搖落三個夏天的驕傲,三個美麗的春天隨季節的過程變成黃色的秋天,三個四月的香氣在三個炎熱的六月燃燒,自從我第一次看到你清新,而你仍然青翠。

passages.original:
Ah! yet doth beauty like a dial-hand,
Steal from his figure, and no pace perceiv’d;
passages.vernacular: 啊!然而美貌好似日晷指針,從佢嘅數字偷走,卻覺察不到步伐;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!然而美貌好像日晷指針,從他的數字偷走,卻覺察不到步伐;

passages.original:
So your sweet hue, which methinks still doth stand,
Hath motion, and mine eye may be deceiv’d:
passages.vernacular: 所以你甜美嘅膚色,我覺得仍然站住,有動作,而我嘅眼睛可能被欺騙:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你甜美的膚色,我覺得仍然站住,有動作,而我的眼睛可能被欺騙:

passages.original: For fear of which, hear this thou age unbred:
passages.vernacular: 為怕呢個,聽呀,未出生嘅時代:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為怕這個,聽啊,未出生的時代:

passages.original: Ere you were born was beauty’s summer dead.
passages.vernacular: 在你出生之前,美嘅夏天已經死咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在你出生之前,美的夏天已經死了。

passages.title: Sonnet 105
passages.original:
Let not my love be call’d idolatry,
Nor my beloved as an idol show,
Since all alike my songs and praises be
To one, of one, still such, and ever so.
passages.vernacular: 唔好稱我嘅愛為偶像崇拜,亦唔好將我愛人當作偶像展示,因為我所有嘅歌同讚美都一樣,對一個,關於一個,永遠如此,一直如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要稱我的愛為偶像崇拜,也不要將我愛人當作偶像展示,因為我所有的歌和讚美都一樣,對一個,關於一個,永遠如此,一直如此。

passages.original:
Kind is my love to-day, to-morrow kind,
Still constant in a wondrous excellence;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅愛今日仁慈,聽日仁慈,在奇妙嘅卓越中仍然恆定;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的愛今天仁慈,明天仁慈,在奇妙的卓越中仍然恆定;

passages.original:
Therefore my verse to constancy confin’d,
One thing expressing, leaves out difference.
passages.vernacular: 所以我嘅詩局限於恆定,表達一件事,省去差別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我的詩局限於恆定,表達一件事,省去差別。

passages.original:
‘Fair, kind, and true,’ is all my argument,
‘Fair, kind, and true,’ varying to other words;
passages.vernacular: 「美、善、真」係我所有嘅主題,「美、善、真」變換成其他嘅字;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美、善、真」是我所有的主題,「美、善、真」變換成其他的字;

passages.original:
And in this change is my invention spent,
Three themes in one, which wondrous scope affords.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅創作就花喺這個變化中,三個主題合一,提供奇妙嘅範圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的創作就花在這個變化中,三個主題合一,提供奇妙的範圍。

passages.original:
Fair, kind, and true, have often liv’d alone,
Which three till now, never kept seat in one.
passages.vernacular: 美、善、真,經常獨自存在,呢三樣直到而家從未同居一處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美、善、真,經常獨自存在,這三樣直到現在從未同居一處。

passages.title: Sonnet 106
passages.original:
When in the chronicle of wasted time
I see descriptions of the fairest wights,
And beauty making beautiful old rime,
In praise of ladies dead and lovely knights,
Then, in the blazon of sweet beauty’s best,
Of hand, of foot, of lip, of eye, of brow,
I see their antique pen would have express’d
Even such a beauty as you master now.
passages.vernacular: 當我喺浪費時間嘅編年史中,見到最美嘅人嘅描述,美貌令古老嘅詩變美,讚美已故嘅女士同可愛嘅騎士,然後在甜美嘅美貌最好部分嘅紋章中,手、腳、唇、眼、額,我見到佢哋古老嘅筆本來會表達,甚至像你而家掌握嘅這種美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我在浪費時間的編年史中,看到最美的人的描述,美貌使古老的詩變美,讚美已故的女士和可愛的騎士,然後在甜美的美貌最好部分的紋章中,手、腳、唇、眼、額,我看到他們古老的筆本來會表達,甚至像你現在掌握的這種美。

passages.original:
So all their praises are but prophecies
Of this our time, all you prefiguring;
passages.vernacular: 所以佢哋所有嘅讚美只不過係我哋這個時代嘅預言,全部預示著你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他們所有的讚美只不過是我們這個時代的預言,全部預示著你;

passages.original:
And for they looked but with divining eyes,
They had not skill enough your worth to sing:
passages.vernacular: 因為佢哋只用預言嘅眼睛看,冇足夠技巧歌頌你嘅價值:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他們只用預言的眼睛看,沒足夠技巧歌頌你的價值:

passages.original:
For we, which now behold these present days,
Have eyes to wonder, but lack tongues to praise.
passages.vernacular: 因為我哋而家看見這些當下嘅日子,有眼睛去驚嘆,卻欠缺舌頭去讚美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我們現在看見這些當下的日子,有眼睛去驚嘆,卻欠缺舌頭去讚美。

passages.title: Sonnet 107
passages.original:
Not mine own fears, nor the prophetic soul
Of the wide world dreaming on things to come,
Can yet the lease of my true love control,
Supposed as forfeit to a confin’d doom.
passages.vernacular: 無論係我自己嘅恐懼,還是廣闊世界夢想未來事物嘅預言之靈魂,都未能控制我真愛嘅租期,被假設為被限定嘅厄運所沒收。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論是我自己的恐懼,還是廣闊世界夢想未來事物的預言之靈魂,都未能控制我真愛的租期,被假設為被限定的厄運所沒收。

passages.original:
The mortal moon hath her eclipse endur’d,
And the sad augurs mock their own presage;
passages.vernacular: 凡人嘅月亮已經捱過佢嘅蝕,悲傷嘅占卜師嘲笑自己嘅預兆;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凡人的月亮已經挨過她的蝕,悲傷的占卜師嘲笑自己的預兆;

passages.original:
Incertainties now crown themselves assur’d,
And peace proclaims olives of endless age.
passages.vernacular: 不確定嘅而家為自己加冕為確定,和平宣布無盡年代嘅橄欖:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不確定的現在為自己加冕為確定,和平宣布無盡年代的橄欖:

passages.original:
Now with the drops of this most balmy time,
My love looks fresh, and Death to me subscribes,
Since, spite of him, I’ll live in this poor rime,
While he insults o’er dull and speechless tribes:
passages.vernacular: 而家憑這個最芬芳時代嘅水滴,我嘅愛看來清新,死亡向我屈服,因為不顧佢,我會活喺呢首貧乏嘅詩中,而佢侮辱遲鈍無言嘅族群:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在憑這個最芬芳時代的水滴,我的愛看來清新,死亡向我屈服,因為不顧他,我會活在這首貧乏的詩中,而他侮辱遲鈍無言的族群:

passages.original:
And thou in this shalt find thy monument,
When tyrants’ crests and tombs of brass are spent.
passages.vernacular: 你喺呢首詩中會找到你嘅紀念碑,當暴君嘅冠冕同銅墳墓都耗盡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在這首詩中會找到你的紀念碑,當暴君的冠冕和銅墳墓都耗盡。

passages.title: Sonnet 108
passages.original:
What’s in the brain, that ink may character,
Which hath not figur’d to thee my true spirit?
passages.vernacular: 頭腦裡有咩,墨水可以描繪,而未曾向你描畫我真正嘅心靈?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭腦裡有什麼,墨水可以描繪,而未曾向你描畫我真正的心靈?

passages.original:
What’s new to speak, what now to register,
That may express my love, or thy dear merit?
passages.vernacular: 有咩新嘢可講,而家有咩可記錄,可以表達我嘅愛,或你親愛嘅功德?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有什麼新東西可說,現在有什麼可記錄,可以表達我的愛,或你親愛的功德?

passages.original:
Nothing, sweet boy; but yet, like prayers divine,
I must each day say o’er the very same;
passages.vernacular: 冇,甜蜜嘅男孩;不過,如神聖嘅禱告,我必須每日重複完全一樣嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,甜蜜的男孩;不過,如神聖的禱告,我必須每天重複完全一樣的;

passages.original:
Counting no old thing old, thou mine, I thine,
Even as when first I hallow’d thy fair name.
passages.vernacular: 唔當任何舊嘢為舊,你屬於我,我屬於你,正如我第一次尊你嘅美名時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不當任何舊東西為舊,你屬於我,我屬於你,正如我第一次尊你的美名時。

passages.original:
So that eternal love in love’s fresh case,
Weighs not the dust and injury of age,
Nor gives to necessary wrinkles place,
But makes antiquity for aye his page;
passages.vernacular: 所以永恆嘅愛,在愛嘅新外殼中,唔計較年老嘅塵土同傷害,亦唔畀必然嘅皺紋位置,而令古老永遠做佢嘅侍從;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以永恆的愛,在愛的新外殼中,不計較年老的塵土和傷害,也不給必然的皺紋位置,而使古老永遠做他的侍從;

passages.original:
Finding the first conceit of love there bred,
Where time and outward form would show it dead.
passages.vernacular: 發現愛嘅最初構想在那裡孕育,而時間同外在形式似乎顯示佢已死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發現愛的最初構想在那裡孕育,而時間和外在形式似乎顯示它已死。

passages.title: Sonnet 109
passages.original:
O! never say that I was false of heart,
Though absence seem’d my flame to qualify,
As easy might I from my self depart
As from my soul which in thy breast doth lie:
passages.vernacular: 啊!永遠唔好講我心虛假,雖然缺席似乎令我嘅火焰減弱,我離開自己,同離開躺喺你胸中嘅靈魂,一樣容易:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!永遠不要說我心虛假,雖然缺席似乎使我的火焰減弱,我離開自己,與離開躺在你胸中的靈魂,一樣容易:

passages.original:
That is my home of love: if I have rang’d,
Like him that travels, I return again;
passages.vernacular: 那就係我愛嘅家:如果我曾漫遊,好似旅行者,我又返嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就是我愛的家:如果我曾漫遊,好像旅行者,我又回來;

passages.original:
Just to the time, not with the time exchang’d,
So that myself bring water for my stain.
passages.vernacular: 準時,冇隨時間而改變,所以我自己帶水洗我嘅污點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 準時,沒隨時間而改變,所以我自己帶水洗我的污點。

passages.original:
Never believe though in my nature reign’d,
All frailties that besiege all kinds of blood,
That it could so preposterously be stain’d,
To leave for nothing all thy sum of good;
passages.vernacular: 雖然在我本性中統治著圍攻各種血液嘅所有軟弱,都唔好相信佢可以咁荒謬地被玷污,而為虛無拋棄你全部嘅善;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然在我本性中統治著圍攻各種血液的所有軟弱,都不要相信它可以這麼荒謬地被玷污,而為虛無拋棄你全部的善;

passages.original:
For nothing this wide universe I call,
Save thou, my rose, in it thou art my all.
passages.vernacular: 我稱這個廣闊嘅宇宙為虛無,除咗你,我嘅玫瑰,在其中你係我嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我稱這個廣闊的宇宙為虛無,除了你,我的玫瑰,在其中你是我的一切。

passages.title: Sonnet 110
passages.original:
Alas! ’tis true, I have gone here and there,
And made my self a motley to the view,
Gor’d mine own thoughts, sold cheap what is most dear,
Made old offences of affections new;
passages.vernacular: 唉!係真嘅,我到處去過,令自己喺眾人眼中成為小丑,刺傷自己嘅思想,將最珍貴嘅賤賣,將新感情變成舊冒犯;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉!是真的,我到處去過,使自己在眾人眼中成為小丑,刺傷自己的思想,將最珍貴的賤賣,將新感情變成舊冒犯;

passages.original:
Most true it is, that I have look’d on truth
Askance and strangely; but, by all above,
These blenches gave my heart another youth,
And worse essays prov’d thee my best of love.
passages.vernacular: 最真嘅係,我曾斜眼奇怪咁看真理;不過憑天上一切發誓,這些閃避給我嘅心另一次青春,而較壞嘅嘗試證明你係我最好嘅愛:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最真的是,我曾斜眼奇怪地看真理;不過憑天上一切發誓,這些閃避給我的心另一次青春,而較壞的嘗試證明你是我最好的愛:

passages.original: Now all is done, save what shall have no end:
passages.vernacular: 而家一切完成,除咗冇終結嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一切完成,除了沒終結的:

passages.original:
Mine appetite I never more will grind
On newer proof, to try an older friend,
A god in love, to whom I am confin’d.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅食慾我再唔會磨向更新嘅證明,去考驗一位更舊嘅朋友,一位愛中嘅神,我被限定於他:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的食慾我再不會磨向更新的證明,去考驗一位更舊的朋友,一位愛中的神,我被限定於他:

passages.original:
Then give me welcome, next my heaven the best,
Even to thy pure and most most loving breast.
passages.vernacular: 咁歡迎我啦,僅次於我嘅天堂最好嘅,甚至歡迎我入你純潔、最最有愛嘅胸膛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那歡迎我吧,僅次於我的天堂最好的,甚至歡迎我進你純潔、最最有愛的胸膛。

passages.title: Sonnet 111
passages.original:
O! for my sake do you with Fortune chide,
The guilty goddess of my harmful deeds,
That did not better for my life provide
Than public means which public manners breeds.
passages.vernacular: 啊!為咗我,你同命運爭吵吧,佢係我有害行為嘅有罪女神,佢冇為我嘅生計提供更好,只畀咗滋生公眾習氣嘅公眾手段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!為了我,你與命運爭吵吧,她是我有害行為的有罪女神,她沒為我的生計提供更好,只給了滋生公眾習氣的公眾手段。

passages.original:
Thence comes it that my name receives a brand,
And almost thence my nature is subdu’d
To what it works in, like the dyer’s hand:
passages.vernacular: 因此我嘅名字受到烙印,幾乎因此我嘅本性被壓抑到順應佢所從事嘅,好似染匠嘅手:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此我的名字受到烙印,幾乎因此我的本性被壓抑到順應它所從事的,好像染匠的手:

passages.original: Pity me, then, and wish I were renew’d;
passages.vernacular: 咁可憐我吧,並希望我被更新;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可憐我吧,並希望我被更新;

passages.original:
Whilst, like a willing patient, I will drink,
Potions of eisel ’gainst my strong infection;
passages.vernacular: 而我,好似一個願意嘅病人,會飲醋嘅藥水對抗我強烈嘅感染;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我,好像一個願意的病人,會飲醋的藥水對抗我強烈的感染;

passages.original:
No bitterness that I will bitter think,
Nor double penance, to correct correction.
passages.vernacular: 冇任何苦味我會覺得苦,亦唔會覺得雙重懺悔,去矯正矯正。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒任何苦味我會覺得苦,也不會覺得雙重懺悔,去矯正矯正。

passages.original:
Pity me then, dear friend, and I assure ye,
Even that your pity is enough to cure me.
passages.vernacular: 咁可憐我吧,親愛嘅朋友,我向你保證,甚至你嘅憐憫已經足夠醫好我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可憐我吧,親愛的朋友,我向你保證,甚至你的憐憫已經足夠醫好我。

passages.title: Sonnet 112
passages.original:
Your love and pity doth the impression fill,
Which vulgar scandal stamp’d upon my brow;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅愛同憐憫填滿庸俗嘅醜聞蓋在我額頭上嘅印記;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的愛和憐憫填滿庸俗的醜聞蓋在我額頭上的印記;

passages.original:
For what care I who calls me well or ill,
So you o’er-green my bad, my good allow?
passages.vernacular: 因為我在乎邊個話我好或壞,只要你用青綠蓋過我嘅壞,承認我嘅好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我在乎誰說我好或壞,只要你用青綠蓋過我的壞,承認我的好?

passages.original:
You are my all-the-world, and I must strive
To know my shames and praises from your tongue;
passages.vernacular: 你係我嘅全世界,我必須努力從你嘅舌頭知道我嘅羞恥同讚美;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是我的全世界,我必須努力從你的舌頭知道我的羞恥和讚美;

passages.original:
None else to me, nor I to none alive,
That my steel’d sense or changes right or wrong.
passages.vernacular: 對我來講冇其他人,我對在生嘅人亦然,能夠改變我鋼鐵般嘅感覺,無論對錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說沒其他人,我對在生的人也然,能夠改變我鋼鐵般的感覺,無論對錯。

passages.original:
In so profound abysm I throw all care
Of others’ voices, that my adder’s sense
To critic and to flatterer stopped are.
passages.vernacular: 我將所有對別人聲音嘅關心扔入咁深嘅深淵,以致我毒蛇般嘅感覺對批評者同奉承者都堵住咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我將所有對別人聲音的關心扔進這麼深的深淵,以致我毒蛇般的感覺對批評者和奉承者都堵住了。

passages.original: Mark how with my neglect I do dispense:
passages.vernacular: 留意我點樣用我嘅忽視來豁免:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意我怎樣用我的忽視來豁免:

passages.original:
You are so strongly in my purpose bred,
That all the world besides methinks are dead.
passages.vernacular: 你咁強烈孕育喺我嘅目的中,以致我覺得世上其餘所有人都死咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這麼強烈孕育在我的目的中,以致我覺得世上其餘所有人都死了。

passages.title: Sonnet 113
passages.original: Since I left you, mine eye is in my mind;
passages.vernacular: 自從我離開你,我嘅眼睛在我嘅頭腦裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我離開你,我的眼睛在我的頭腦裡;

passages.vernacular: 引領我四處走動嘅,分擔佢嘅功能並部分失明,似乎在看,實際上冇看;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 引領我四處走動的,分擔他的功能並部分失明,似乎在看,實際上沒看;

passages.original:
For it no form delivers to the heart
Of bird, of flower, or shape which it doth latch:
passages.vernacular: 因為佢冇向心傳遞任何鳥、花,或佢捕捉到嘅形狀嘅形象:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為它沒向心傳遞任何鳥、花,或它捕捉到的形狀的形象:

passages.original:
Of his quick objects hath the mind no part,
Nor his own vision holds what it doth catch;
passages.vernacular: 頭腦對佢迅速嘅對象冇一份,佢自己嘅視覺亦唔保留佢所捕捉嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭腦對他迅速的對象沒一份,他自己的視覺也不保留他所捕捉的;

passages.original:
