For if it see the rud’st or gentlest sight,
The most sweet favour or deformed’st creature,
The mountain or the sea, the day or night:
passages.vernacular: 因為如果佢見到最粗魯或最溫柔嘅景象,最甜美嘅容貌或最畸形嘅生物,山或海,日或夜:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果他看到最粗魯或最溫柔的景象,最甜美的容貌或最畸形的生物,山或海,日或夜:

passages.original: The crow, or dove, it shapes them to your feature.
passages.vernacular: 烏鴉或鴿子,佢都將佢哋塑造成你嘅樣貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 烏鴉或鴿子,他都將它們塑造成你的樣貌。

passages.original:
Incapable of more, replete with you,
My most true mind thus maketh mine untrue.
passages.vernacular: 無法容納更多,充滿咗你,我最真誠嘅頭腦就咁令我不真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無法容納更多,充滿了你,我最真誠的頭腦就這樣使我不真。

passages.title: Sonnet 114
passages.original:
Or whether doth my mind, being crown’d with you,
Drink up the monarch’s plague, this flattery?
passages.vernacular: 或者,我嘅頭腦被你加冕,係咪飲下君主嘅瘟疫,呢種奉承?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,我的頭腦被你加冕,是不是飲下君主的瘟疫,這種奉承?

passages.original:
Or whether shall I say, mine eye saith true,
And that your love taught it this alchemy,
To make of monsters and things indigest
Such cherubins as your sweet self resemble,
Creating every bad a perfect best,
As fast as objects to his beams assemble?
passages.vernacular: 或者我應該講,我嘅眼睛講真話,而你嘅愛教佢呢種煉金術,將怪物同未消化嘅東西,造成似你甜美自己嘅小天使,將每個壞都造成完美最好,同對象向佢光線聚集一樣快?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者我應該說,我的眼睛說真話,而你的愛教它這種煉金術,將怪物和未消化的東西,造成像你甜美自己的小天使,將每個壞都造成完美最好,與對象向他光線聚集一樣快?

passages.original:
O! ’tis the first, ’tis flattery in my seeing,
And my great mind most kingly drinks it up:
passages.vernacular: 啊!係頭一個,係我視覺中嘅奉承,而我偉大嘅頭腦最像君王咁飲下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!是頭一個,是我視覺中的奉承,而我偉大的頭腦最像君王地飲下:

passages.original:
Mine eye well knows what with his gust is ’greeing,
And to his palate doth prepare the cup:
passages.vernacular: 我嘅眼睛清楚知道咩合佢嘅口味,並為佢嘅味覺準備杯:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的眼睛清楚知道什麼合他的口味,並為他的味覺準備杯:

passages.original:
If it be poison’d, ’tis the lesser sin
That mine eye loves it and doth first begin.
passages.vernacular: 如果杯有毒,罪較輕,因為我嘅眼睛愛佢並首先開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果杯有毒,罪較輕,因為我的眼睛愛它並首先開始。

passages.title: Sonnet 115
passages.original:
Those lines that I before have writ do lie,
Even those that said I could not love you dearer:
passages.vernacular: 我之前寫過嘅詩行都在撒謊,甚至那些話我不能更愛你嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我之前寫過的詩行都在撒謊,甚至那些說我不能更愛你的:

passages.original:
Yet then my judgement knew no reason why
My most full flame should afterwards burn clearer.
passages.vernacular: 然而當時我嘅判斷唔知道有咩理由,我最飽滿嘅火焰之後應該燒得更清澈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而當時我的判斷不知道有什麼理由,我最飽滿的火焰之後應該燒得更清澈。

passages.original:
But reckoning Time, whose million’d accidents
Creep in ’twixt vows, and change decrees of kings,
Tan sacred beauty, blunt the sharp’st intents,
Divert strong minds to the course of altering things;
passages.vernacular: 不過計算中嘅時間,其百萬次意外爬入誓言之間,改變君王嘅法令,曬黑神聖嘅美貌,磨鈍最尖銳嘅意圖,將堅強嘅頭腦轉向改變事物嘅進程;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過計算中的時間,其百萬次意外爬進誓言之間,改變君王的法令,曬黑神聖的美貌,磨鈍最尖銳的意圖,將堅強的頭腦轉向改變事物的進程;

passages.original:
Alas! why fearing of Time’s tyranny,
Might I not then say, ‘Now I love you best,’
When I was certain o’er incertainty,
Crowning the present, doubting of the rest?
passages.vernacular: 唉!因為怕時間嘅暴政,我點解唔可以那時講「而家我最愛你」,當我對不確定肯定,為當下加冕,懷疑其餘?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉!因為怕時間的暴政,我為什麼不可以那時說「現在我最愛你」,當我對不確定肯定,為當下加冕,懷疑其餘?

passages.original:
Love is a babe, then might I not say so,
To give full growth to that which still doth grow?
passages.vernacular: 愛係嬰兒,咁我可唔可以咁講,畀仍在生長嘅東西完全成長?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛是嬰兒,那我可不可以這樣說,給仍在生長的東西完全成長?

passages.title: Sonnet 116
passages.original:
Let me not to the marriage of true minds
Admit impediments. Love is not love
Which alters when it alteration finds,
Or bends with the remover to remove:
passages.vernacular: 唔好讓我對真心嘅婚姻承認障礙。愛唔係愛,如果佢發現改變就改變,或隨移開者而移開:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要讓我對真心的婚姻承認障礙。愛不是愛,如果他發現改變就改變,或隨移開者而移開:

passages.original:
O, no! it is an ever-fixed mark,
That looks on tempests and is never shaken;
passages.vernacular: 啊,不!佢係永遠固定嘅標記,望住風暴而從不動搖;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,不!它是永遠固定的標記,望著風暴而從不動搖;

passages.original:
It is the star to every wandering bark,
Whose worth’s unknown, although his height be taken.
passages.vernacular: 佢係每艘漂泊小船嘅星,佢嘅價值未知,雖然佢嘅高度被量度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是每艘漂泊小船的星,它的價值未知,雖然它的高度被量度。

passages.original:
Love’s not Time’s fool, though rosy lips and cheeks
Within his bending sickle’s compass come;
passages.vernacular: 愛唔係時間嘅傻瓜,雖然玫瑰色嘅嘴唇同臉頰落入佢彎曲鐮刀嘅範圍;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛不是時間的傻瓜,雖然玫瑰色的嘴唇和臉頰落入他彎曲鐮刀的範圍;

passages.original:
Love alters not with his brief hours and weeks,
But bears it out even to the edge of doom.
passages.vernacular: 愛唔隨佢短暫嘅時辰同星期而改變,而係一直承受到末日審判嘅邊緣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛不隨他短暫的時辰和星期而改變,而是一直承受到末日審判的邊緣。

passages.original:
If this be error and upon me prov’d,
I never writ, nor no man ever lov’d.
passages.vernacular: 如果這是錯誤,並在我身上被證明,我從未寫過,亦冇人曾愛過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這是錯誤,並在我身上被證明,我從未寫過,也沒人曾愛過。

passages.title: Sonnet 117
passages.original:
Accuse me thus: that I have scanted all,
Wherein I should your great deserts repay,
Forgot upon your dearest love to call,
Whereto all bonds do tie me day by day;
passages.vernacular: 咁樣控告我吧:我吝嗇咗所有,本應用來回報你偉大功績嘅;忘記呼求你最親愛嘅愛,而所有契約日復一日將我綁於此;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣控告我吧:我吝嗇了所有,本應用來回報你偉大功績的;忘記呼求你最親愛的愛,而所有契約日復一日將我綁於此;

passages.original:
That I have frequent been with unknown minds,
And given to time your own dear-purchas’d right;
passages.vernacular: 我經常同陌生嘅頭腦在一起,將你親手買來嘅權利畀咗時間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我經常與陌生的頭腦在一起,將你親手買來的權利給了時間;

passages.original:
That I have hoisted sail to all the winds
Which should transport me farthest from your sight.
passages.vernacular: 我向所有風揚帆,本應將我運送到離你視線最遠處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向所有風揚帆,本應將我運送到離你視線最遠處。

passages.original:
Book both my wilfulness and errors down,
And on just proof surmise, accumulate;
passages.vernacular: 將我嘅任性同錯誤都記下,並憑正當證據推測、累積;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將我的任性和錯誤都記下,並憑正當證據推測、累積;

passages.original:
Bring me within the level of your frown,
But shoot not at me in your waken’d hate;
passages.vernacular: 將我帶到你皺眉嘅水平內,不過唔好喺你被喚醒嘅恨中射我:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將我帶到你皺眉的水平內,不過不要在你被喚醒的恨中射我:

passages.original:
Since my appeal says I did strive to prove
The constancy and virtue of your love.
passages.vernacular: 因為我嘅申訴話我曾努力證明你愛嘅恆定同美德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我的申訴說我曾努力證明你愛的恆定和美德。

passages.title: Sonnet 118
passages.original:
Like as, to make our appetite more keen,
With eager compounds we our palate urge;
passages.vernacular: 好似為令我哋食慾更敏銳,我哋用強烈嘅混合物刺激味覺;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像為使我們食慾更敏銳,我們用強烈的混合物刺激味覺;

passages.original:
As, to prevent our maladies unseen,
We sicken to shun sickness when we purge;
passages.vernacular: 好似為預防我哋看不見嘅疾病,我哋喺清腸時令自己生病以避開疾病;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像為預防我們看不見的疾病,我們在清腸時使自己生病以避開疾病;

passages.original:
Even so, being full of your ne’er-cloying sweetness,
To bitter sauces did I frame my feeding;
passages.vernacular: 同樣,充滿咗你永不令人厭膩嘅甜美,我將我嘅飲食擬向苦澀嘅醬汁;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同樣,充滿了你永不使人厭膩的甜美,我將我的飲食擬向苦澀的醬汁;

passages.original:
And, sick of welfare, found a kind of meetness
To be diseas’d, ere that there was true needing.
passages.vernacular: 厭倦安康,找到某種合適去生病,喺真正需要之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 厭倦安康,找到某種合適去生病,在真正需要之前。

passages.original:
Thus policy in love, to anticipate
The ills that were not, grew to faults assur’d,
And brought to medicine a healthful state
Which, rank of goodness, would by ill be cur’d;
passages.vernacular: 就咁愛中嘅策略,預先防備不存在嘅惡,變成確實嘅過失,並為醫藥帶來一個健康嘅狀態,佢因過分良善,會被惡治癒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣愛中的策略,預先防備不存在的惡,變成確實的過失,並為醫藥帶來一個健康的狀態,它因過分良善,會被惡治癒;

passages.original:
But thence I learn and find the lesson true,
Drugs poison him that so fell sick of you.
passages.vernacular: 不過從此我學到並發現教訓係真:藥毒害咁樣因你而病倒嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過從此我學到並發現教訓是真:藥毒害這樣因你而病倒的人。

passages.title: Sonnet 119
passages.original:
What potions have I drunk of Siren tears,
Distill’d from limbecks foul as hell within,
Applying fears to hopes, and hopes to fears,
Still losing when I saw myself to win!
passages.vernacular: 我飲咗幾多海妖眼淚嘅藥水,從內裡污穢如地獄嘅蒸餾器蒸餾出嚟,將恐懼施於希望,希望施於恐懼,見到自己贏時仍然輸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我飲了多少海妖眼淚的藥水,從內裡污穢如地獄的蒸餾器蒸餾出來,將恐懼施於希望,希望施於恐懼,看到自己贏時仍然輸!

passages.original:
What wretched errors hath my heart committed,
Whilst it hath thought itself so blessed never!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心犯下幾可悲嘅錯誤,當佢以為自己從未咁有福!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心犯下多可悲的錯誤,當它以為自己從未這麼有福!

passages.original:
How have mine eyes out of their spheres been fitted,
In the distraction of this madding fever!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅眼睛喺呢場瘋狂發燒嘅迷亂中,點樣被擠出佢哋嘅眼眶!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的眼睛在這場瘋狂發燒的迷亂中,怎樣被擠出它們的眼眶!

passages.original:
O benefit of ill! now I find true
That better is, by evil still made better;
passages.vernacular: 啊惡嘅益處!我而家發現真係更好,被惡令更好;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊惡的益處!我現在發現真是更好,被惡使更好;

passages.original:
And ruin’d love, when it is built anew,
Grows fairer than at first, more strong, far greater.
passages.vernacular: 而被毀嘅愛,當重新建造,比最初更美,更強,大得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而被毀的愛,當重新建造,比最初更美,更強,大得多。

passages.original:
So I return rebuk’d to my content,
And gain by ill thrice more than I have spent.
passages.vernacular: 所以我被責備後返回我嘅滿足,憑惡得到比我花費嘅多三倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我被責備後回到我的滿足,憑惡得到比我花費的多三倍。

passages.title: Sonnet 120
passages.original:
That you were once unkind befriends me now,
And for that sorrow, which I then did feel,
Needs must I under my transgression bow,
Unless my nerves were brass or hammer’d steel.
passages.vernacular: 你曾經不友善,而家對我有益,因為我當時感到嘅悲傷,我必須在我嘅過犯下低頭,除非我嘅神經係銅或錘打過嘅鋼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你曾經不友善,現在對我有益,因為我當時感到的悲傷,我必須在我的過犯下低頭,除非我的神經是銅或錘打過的鋼。

passages.original:
For if you were by my unkindness shaken,
As I by yours, you’ve pass’d a hell of time;
passages.vernacular: 因為如果你被我嘅不友善震動,好似我被你嘅,你就經歷咗一段地獄般嘅時間;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果你被我的不友善震動,好像我被你的,你就經歷了一段地獄般的時間;

passages.original:
And I, a tyrant, have no leisure taken
To weigh how once I suffer’d in your crime.
passages.vernacular: 而我,一個暴君,冇閒暇去權衡我曾幾咁喺你嘅罪中受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我,一個暴君,沒閒暇去權衡我曾多麼在你的罪中受苦。

passages.original:
O! that our night of woe might have remember’d
My deepest sense, how hard true sorrow hits,
And soon to you, as you to me, then tender’d
The humble salve, which wounded bosoms fits!
passages.vernacular: 啊!願我哋嘅悲傷之夜記得我最深嘅感受,真正嘅悲傷打擊得幾狠,並好快將適合受傷胸膛嘅謙卑藥膏,像你對我一樣,獻畀你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!願我們的悲傷之夜記得我最深的感受,真正的悲傷打擊得多狠,並很快將適合受傷胸膛的謙卑藥膏,像你對我一樣,獻給你!

passages.original: But that your trespass now becomes a fee;
passages.vernacular: 不過你嘅過犯而家成為一筆費用;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你的過犯現在成為一筆費用;

passages.original: Mine ransoms yours, and yours must ransom me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅贖你嘅,而你嘅必須贖我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的贖你的,而你的必須贖我。

passages.title: Sonnet 121
passages.original:
’Tis better to be vile than vile esteem’d,
When not to be receives reproach of being;
passages.vernacular: 寧願卑劣都好過被當作卑劣,當冇存在都受到存在嘅責難;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寧願卑劣也好過被當作卑劣,當不存在都受到存在的責難;

passages.original:
And the just pleasure lost, which is so deem’d
Not by our feeling, but by others’ seeing:
passages.vernacular: 而正當嘅歡愉失去,被如此視為不是憑我哋嘅感覺,而是憑別人嘅看法:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而正當的歡愉失去,被如此視為不是憑我們的感覺,而是憑別人的看法:

passages.original:
For why should others’ false adulterate eyes
Give salutation to my sportive blood?
passages.vernacular: 因為別人虛假、摻雜嘅眼睛,點解要向我嬉戲嘅血液問候?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為別人虛假、摻雜的眼睛,為什麼要向我嬉戲的血液問候?

passages.original:
Or on my frailties why are frailer spies,
Which in their wills count bad what I think good?
passages.vernacular: 或者對我嘅軟弱,點解有更軟弱嘅探子,佢哋憑佢哋嘅意願,將我認為好嘅算作壞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者對我的軟弱,為什麼有更軟弱的探子,他們憑他們的意願,將我認為好的算作壞?

passages.original:
No, I am that I am, and they that level
At my abuses reckon up their own:
passages.vernacular: 不,我就係我所是,而那些瞄準我嘅濫用嘅人,數算佢哋自己嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我就是我所是,而那些瞄準我的濫用的人,數算他們自己的:

passages.original: I may be straight though they themselves be bevel;
passages.vernacular: 我可能係正直嘅,雖然佢哋自己係斜嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可能是正直的,雖然他們自己是斜的;

passages.original: By their rank thoughts, my deeds must not be shown;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅行為不應由佢哋腐臭嘅思想來顯示;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的行為不應由他們腐臭的思想來顯示;

passages.original:
Unless this general evil they maintain,
All men are bad and in their badness reign.
passages.vernacular: 除非佢哋堅持這個普遍嘅惡:所有人都壞,並在佢哋嘅壞中稱王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除非他們堅持這個普遍的惡:所有人都壞,並在他們的壞中稱王。

passages.title: Sonnet 122
passages.original:
Thy gift, thy tables, are within my brain
Full character’d with lasting memory,
Which shall above that idle rank remain,
Beyond all date; even to eternity:
passages.vernacular: 你嘅禮物,你嘅記事板,就喺我嘅頭腦裡,佈滿持久嘅記憶刻字,佢會超越嗰個閒置嘅等級,超越所有日期,甚至到永恆:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的禮物,你的記事板,就在我的頭腦裡,佈滿持久的記憶刻字,它會超越那個閒置的等級,超越所有日期,甚至到永恆:

passages.original:
Or, at the least, so long as brain and heart
Have faculty by nature to subsist;
passages.vernacular: 或者,至少,只要頭腦同心天生有能力存續;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,至少,只要頭腦和心天生有能力存續;

passages.original:
Till each to raz’d oblivion yield his part
Of thee, thy record never can be miss’d.
passages.vernacular: 直到各自向被夷平嘅遺忘交出佢哋對你嘅一份,你嘅記錄永遠不會被錯過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到各自向被夷平的遺忘交出他們對你的一份,你的記錄永遠不會被錯過。

passages.original:
That poor retention could not so much hold,
Nor need I tallies thy dear love to score;
passages.vernacular: 嗰個可憐嘅記錄本唔可以容納咁多,我亦唔需要計數籤去記你親愛嘅愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個可憐的記錄本不可以容納這麼多,我也不需要計數籤去記你親愛的愛;

passages.original:
Therefore to give them from me was I bold,
To trust those tables that receive thee more:
passages.vernacular: 所以我大膽將佢哋從我身邊送走,信任嗰啲容納你更多嘅記事板:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我大膽將它們從我身邊送走,信任那些容納你更多的記事板:

passages.original:
To keep an adjunct to remember thee
Were to import forgetfulness in me.
passages.vernacular: 保留一個附屬品去記住你,就係向我引入遺忘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保留一個附屬品去記住你,就是向我引入遺忘。

passages.title: Sonnet 123
passages.original: No, Time, thou shalt not boast that I do change:
passages.vernacular: 唔,時間,你唔可以誇口我改變:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,時間,你不可以誇口我改變:

passages.original:
Thy pyramids built up with newer might
To me are nothing novel, nothing strange;
passages.vernacular: 你用更新嘅力量建起嘅金字塔,對我來講冇咩新奇,冇咩奇怪;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你用更新的力量建起的金字塔,對我來說沒什麼新奇,沒什麼奇怪;

passages.original: They are but dressings of a former sight.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋只不過係從前景象嘅重新裝扮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們只不過是從前景象的重新裝扮。

passages.original:
Our dates are brief, and therefore we admire
What thou dost foist upon us that is old;
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅日子短暫,所以我哋讚嘆你偷偷塞畀我哋嘅舊嘢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的日子短暫,所以我們讚嘆你偷偷塞給我們的舊東西;

passages.original:
And rather make them born to our desire
Than think that we before have heard them told.
passages.vernacular: 寧願將佢哋說成為我哋嘅慾望而生,而唔認為我哋以前聽過佢哋被講述。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寧願將它們說成為我們的慾望而生,而不認為我們以前聽過它們被講述。

passages.original:
Thy registers and thee I both defy,
Not wondering at the present nor the past,
For thy records and what we see doth lie,
Made more or less by thy continual haste.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅記錄同你,我兩者都蔑視,對當下同過去都唔驚奇,因為你嘅記錄同我哋所見都在撒謊,被你持續嘅匆忙造得或多或少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的記錄和你,我兩者都蔑視,對當下和過去都不驚奇,因為你的記錄和我們所見都在撒謊,被你持續的匆忙造得或多或少。

passages.original: This I do vow and this shall ever be;
passages.vernacular: 我發誓呢個,呢將永遠如此;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發誓這個,這將永遠如此;

passages.original: I will be true despite thy scythe and thee.
passages.vernacular: 我會真誠,不顧你嘅鐮刀同你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會真誠,不顧你的鐮刀和你。

passages.title: Sonnet 124
passages.original:
If my dear love were but the child of state,
It might for Fortune’s bastard be unfather’d,
As subject to Time’s love or to Time’s hate,
Weeds among weeds, or flowers with flowers gather’d.
passages.vernacular: 如果我親愛嘅愛只係地位嘅孩子,佢可能被當作命運嘅私生子而無父,受時間嘅愛或恨支配,雜草中嘅雜草,或花同花一齊被採:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我親愛的愛只是地位的孩子,它可能被當作命運的私生子而無父,受時間的愛或恨支配,雜草中的雜草,或花和花一起被採:

passages.original: No, it was builded far from accident;
passages.vernacular: 不,佢建造得遠離意外;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,它建造得遠離意外;

passages.original:
It suffers not in smiling pomp, nor falls
Under the blow of thralled discontent,
Whereto th’ inviting time our fashion calls:
passages.vernacular: 佢唔因微笑嘅華麗而受苦,亦唔喺被奴役嘅不滿嘅打擊下跌倒,誘人嘅時代呼召我哋嘅風尚去呢種不滿:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不因微笑的華麗而受苦,也不在被奴役的不滿的打擊下跌倒,誘人的時代呼召我們的風尚去這種不滿:

passages.original:
It fears not policy, that heretic,
Which works on leases of short-number’d hours,
But all alone stands hugely politic,
That it nor grows with heat, nor drowns with showers.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔怕權謀,嗰個異端,佢以短暫時辰嘅租約運作,而係獨自巨大咁精明地站住,以致佢既唔因熱而生長,亦唔因陣雨而淹沒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不怕權謀,那個異端,它以短暫時辰的租約運作,而是獨自巨大地精明地站住,以致它既不因熱而生長,也不因陣雨而淹沒。

passages.original:
To this I witness call the fools of time,
Which die for goodness, who have lived for crime.
passages.vernacular: 對此我召喚時間嘅傻瓜作證,佢哋為善而死,卻為罪而生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對此我召喚時間的傻瓜作證,他們為善而死,卻為罪而生。

passages.title: Sonnet 125
passages.original:
Were’t aught to me I bore the canopy,
With my extern the outward honouring,
Or laid great bases for eternity,
Which proves more short than waste or ruining?
passages.vernacular: 如果我撐住華蓋,用我外在嘅外表榮耀,或為永恆打下偉大嘅地基,而佢證明比浪費或毀滅更短,對我有咩意義?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我撐著華蓋,用我外在的外表榮耀,或為永恆打下偉大的地基,而它證明比浪費或毀滅更短,對我有什麼意義?

passages.original:
Have I not seen dwellers on form and favour
Lose all and more by paying too much rent
For compound sweet; forgoing simple savour,
Pitiful thrivers, in their gazing spent?
passages.vernacular: 我冇見過居住於形式同恩寵嘅人,為咗混合嘅甜美付太多租金,而失去所有甚至更多,放棄單純嘅滋味,可憐嘅興旺者,耗盡在凝望中嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒看過居住於形式和恩寵的人,為了混合的甜美付太多租金,而失去所有甚至更多,放棄單純的滋味,可憐的興旺者,耗盡在凝望中嗎?

passages.original:
No; let me be obsequious in thy heart,
And take thou my oblation, poor but free,
Which is not mix’d with seconds, knows no art,
But mutual render, only me for thee.
passages.vernacular: 唔;讓我喺你心中恭順,接受我嘅供奉,雖然貧乏卻自由,冇混雜次等,唔識技巧,只有互相交付,只有我換你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不;讓我在你心中恭順,接受我的供奉,雖然貧乏卻自由,沒混雜次等,不懂技巧,只有互相交付,只有我換你。

passages.original:
Hence, thou suborned informer! a true soul
When most impeach’d, stands least in thy control.
passages.vernacular: 走開,你呢個被收買嘅告密者!一個真誠嘅靈魂,最被指控時,最少受你控制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,你這個被收買的告密者!一個真誠的靈魂,最被指控時,最少受你控制。

passages.title: Sonnet 126
passages.original:
O thou, my lovely boy, who in thy power
Dost hold Time’s fickle glass, his fickle hour;
passages.vernacular: 啊你,我可愛嘅男孩,你手中握住時間反覆無常嘅鏡子,佢反覆無常嘅時辰;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊你,我可愛的男孩,你手中握著時間反覆無常的鏡子,他反覆無常的時辰;

passages.original:
Who hast by waning grown, and therein show’st
Thy lovers withering, as thy sweet self grow’st.
passages.vernacular: 你憑衰退而成長,並因此顯示你嘅愛人枯萎,而你甜美嘅自己生長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你憑衰退而成長,並因此顯示你的愛人枯萎,而你甜美的自己生長。

passages.original:
If Nature, sovereign mistress over wrack,
As thou goest onwards, still will pluck thee back,
She keeps thee to this purpose, that her skill
May time disgrace and wretched minutes kill.
passages.vernacular: 如果大自然,毀滅嘅君主女主人,隨你向前走,仍然要將你拉回,佢將你留作這個目的,令佢嘅技藝可以羞辱時間並殺死可憐嘅分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果大自然,毀滅的君主女主人,隨你向前走,仍然要將你拉回,她將你留作這個目的,使她的技藝可以羞辱時間並殺死可憐的分鐘。

passages.original: Yet fear her, O thou minion of her pleasure!
passages.vernacular: 不過要怕佢,啊你呢個佢歡愉嘅寵兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過要怕她,啊你這個她歡愉的寵兒!

passages.original: She may detain, but not still keep, her treasure:
passages.vernacular: 佢可以扣留,但唔能夠永遠保留佢嘅寶藏:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她可以扣留,但不能夠永遠保留她的寶藏:

passages.original:
Her audit (though delayed) answered must be,
And her quietus is to render thee.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅審計(雖然延遲)必須被回答,而佢嘅清償就係交還你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的審計(雖然延遲)必須被回答,而她的清償就是交還你。

passages.title: Sonnet 127
passages.original:
In the old age black was not counted fair,
Or if it were, it bore not beauty’s name;
passages.vernacular: 在舊時代,黑色唔被視為美,或者即使係,都唔承載美嘅名字;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在舊時代,黑色不被視為美,或者即使是,也不承載美的名字;

passages.original:
But now is black beauty’s successive heir,
And beauty slander’d with a bastard shame:
passages.vernacular: 不過而家黑色係美嘅繼承人,而美被私生嘅恥辱誹謗:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在黑色是美的繼承人,而美被私生的恥辱誹謗:

passages.original:
For since each hand hath put on Nature’s power,
Fairing the foul with Art’s false borrowed face,
Sweet beauty hath no name, no holy bower,
But is profan’d, if not lives in disgrace.
passages.vernacular: 因為自從每隻手都披上大自然嘅力量,用藝術虛假借來嘅臉美化醜陋,甜美嘅美貌冇名字,冇神聖嘅閨房,而係被褻瀆,如果唔係活在恥辱中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為自從每隻手都披上大自然的力量,用藝術虛假借來的臉美化醜陋,甜美的美貌沒名字,沒神聖的閨房,而是被褻瀆,如果不是活在恥辱中。

passages.original:
Therefore my mistress’ eyes are raven black,
Her eyes so suited, and they mourners seem
At such who, not born fair, no beauty lack,
Sland’ring creation with a false esteem:
passages.vernacular: 所以我情人嘅眼睛係烏鴉般黑,佢嘅眼睛咁穿著,佢哋似乎為嗰啲唔係生來美、卻唔欠缺美嘅人哀悼,他們用虛假嘅評價誹謗造物:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我情人的眼睛是烏鴉般黑,她的眼睛這樣穿著,它們似乎為那些不是生來美、卻不欠缺美的人哀悼,他們用虛假的評價誹謗造物:

passages.original:
Yet so they mourn becoming of their woe,
That every tongue says beauty should look so.
passages.vernacular: 然而佢哋哀悼得咁配合佢哋嘅悲痛,以致每條舌頭都講美應該係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而它們哀悼得這樣配合它們的悲痛,以致每條舌頭都說美應該是這樣。

passages.title: Sonnet 128
passages.original:
How oft when thou, my music, music play’st,
Upon that blessed wood whose motion sounds
With thy sweet fingers when thou gently sway’st
The wiry concord that mine ear confounds,
Do I envy those jacks that nimble leap,
To kiss the tender inward of thy hand,
Whilst my poor lips which should that harvest reap,
At the wood’s boldness by thee blushing stand!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅音樂,你彈音樂時,在嗰塊有福嘅木頭上,當你溫柔咁搖動令我耳朵混亂嘅絲弦和諧時,木頭嘅動作隨你甜美嘅手指發聲,我幾多次妒忌嗰啲敏捷跳動嘅琴鍵,去吻你手嘅柔軟內側,而我可憐嘅嘴唇本應收穫呢份收成,卻對木頭嘅大膽喺你面前臉紅站住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的音樂,你彈音樂時,在那塊有福的木頭上,當你溫柔地搖動使我耳朵混亂的絲弦和諧時,木頭的動作隨你甜美的手指發聲,我多少次妒忌那些敏捷跳動的琴鍵,去吻你手的柔軟內側,而我可憐的嘴唇本應收穫這份收成,卻對木頭的大膽在你面前臉紅站住!

passages.original:
To be so tickled, they would change their state
And situation with those dancing chips,
O’er whom thy fingers walk with gentle gait,
Making dead wood more bless’d than living lips.
passages.vernacular: 被咁樣撓癢,佢哋願意改變處境,同嗰啲舞動嘅木片交換位置,你嘅手指帶住溫柔嘅步伐在佢哋上面行走,令死木頭比活嘴唇更有福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被這樣撓癢,它們願意改變處境,與那些舞動的木片交換位置,你的手指帶著溫柔的步伐在它們上面行走,使死木頭比活嘴唇更有福。

passages.original:
Since saucy jacks so happy are in this,
Give them thy fingers, me thy lips to kiss.
passages.vernacular: 既然放肆嘅琴鍵喺此咁快樂,就將你嘅手指畀佢哋,將你嘅嘴唇畀我吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然放肆的琴鍵在此這麼快樂,就將你的手指給它們,將你的嘴唇給我吻。

passages.title: Sonnet 129
passages.original:
The expense of spirit in a waste of shame
Is lust in action: and till action, lust
Is perjur’d, murderous, bloody, full of blame,
Savage, extreme, rude, cruel, not to trust;
passages.vernacular: 喺羞恥嘅浪費中耗費精神,就係行動中嘅慾望:行動之前,慾望背誓、殺人、流血、充滿罪責、野蠻、極端、粗魯、殘酷、不可信;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在羞恥的浪費中耗費精神,就是行動中的慾望:行動之前,慾望背誓、殺人、流血、充滿罪責、野蠻、極端、粗魯、殘酷、不可信;

passages.original: Enjoy’d no sooner but despised straight;
passages.vernacular: 剛享受就即刻被鄙視;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛享受就立刻被鄙視;

passages.original:
Past reason hunted; and no sooner had,
Past reason hated, as a swallow’d bait,
On purpose laid to make the taker mad:
passages.vernacular: 不講理地被追逐;剛得到,就不講理地被憎恨,好似吞咗嘅餌,特意放置令吞者發瘋:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不講理地被追逐;剛得到,就不講理地被憎恨,好像吞了的餌,特意放置使吞者發瘋:

passages.original: Mad in pursuit and in possession so;
passages.vernacular: 追逐時瘋狂,擁有時都一樣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 追逐時瘋狂,擁有時也一樣;

passages.original: Had, having, and in quest, to have extreme;
passages.vernacular: 已擁有,正擁有,同追求,都要擁有到極端;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已擁有,正擁有,和追求,都要擁有到極端;

passages.original: A bliss in proof, and proved, a very woe;
passages.vernacular: 試驗時係福,試驗過後,係十足嘅苦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 試驗時是福,試驗過後,是十足的苦;

passages.original: Before, a joy propos’d; behind a dream.
passages.vernacular: 之前,係被提出嘅歡愉;之後,係一場夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之前,是被提出的歡愉;之後,是一場夢。

passages.original:
All this the world well knows; yet none knows well
To shun the heaven that leads men to this hell.
passages.vernacular: 所有這些世界都清楚知道;不過冇人懂得避開引人入這個地獄嘅天堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有這些世界都清楚知道;不過沒人懂得避開引人入這個地獄的天堂。

passages.title: Sonnet 130
passages.original: My mistress’ eyes are nothing like the sun;
passages.vernacular: 我情人嘅眼睛一啲都唔似太陽;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我情人的眼睛一點都不像太陽;

passages.original: Coral is far more red, than her lips red:
passages.vernacular: 珊瑚比佢嘅唇紅得多:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 珊瑚比她的唇紅得多:

passages.original: If snow be white, why then her breasts are dun;
passages.vernacular: 如果雪係白,咁佢嘅胸就係灰褐;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果雪是白,那她的胸就是灰褐;

passages.original: If hairs be wires, black wires grow on her head.
passages.vernacular: 如果頭髮係金屬絲,黑色嘅金屬絲長喺佢頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果頭髮是金屬絲,黑色的金屬絲長在她頭上。

passages.original:
I have seen roses damask’d, red and white,
But no such roses see I in her cheeks;
passages.vernacular: 我見過大馬士革玫瑰,紅同白,不過我喺佢臉頰上見唔到咁嘅玫瑰;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我見過大馬士革玫瑰,紅和白,不過我在她臉頰上看不到這樣的玫瑰;

passages.original:
And in some perfumes is there more delight
Than in the breath that from my mistress reeks.
passages.vernacular: 有些香水比我情人呼出嘅氣息更令人歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些香水比我情人呼出的氣息更令人歡喜。

passages.original:
I love to hear her speak, yet well I know
That music hath a far more pleasing sound:
passages.vernacular: 我愛聽佢講話,不過我清楚知道音樂有更悅耳嘅聲音:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛聽她說話,不過我清楚知道音樂有更悅耳的聲音:

passages.original: I grant I never saw a goddess go;
passages.vernacular: 我承認我從未見過女神行路;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認我從未見過女神行路;

passages.original: My mistress, when she walks, treads on the ground:
passages.vernacular: 我嘅情人行路時,踩喺地上:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的情人行路時,踩在地上:

passages.original:
And yet by heaven, I think my love as rare,
As any she belied with false compare.
passages.vernacular: 然而憑天發誓,我認為我嘅愛人同任何被虛假比較誹謗嘅女人一樣稀罕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而憑天發誓,我認為我的愛人與任何被虛假比較誹謗的女人一樣稀罕。

passages.title: Sonnet 131
passages.original:
Thou art as tyrannous, so as thou art,
As those whose beauties proudly make them cruel;
passages.vernacular: 你係暴君,正如你就係咁,同嗰啲因美貌而驕傲咁殘忍嘅人一樣;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是暴君,正如你就是這樣,與那些因美貌而驕傲地殘忍的人一樣;

passages.original:
For well thou know’st to my dear doting heart
Thou art the fairest and most precious jewel.
passages.vernacular: 因為你清楚知道,對我親愛癡迷嘅心,你係最美最珍貴嘅珠寶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你清楚知道,對我親愛癡迷的心,你是最美最珍貴的珠寶。

passages.original:
Yet, in good faith, some say that thee behold,
Thy face hath not the power to make love groan;
passages.vernacular: 然而,老實講,有些看你嘅人話,你嘅臉冇力量令愛呻吟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,老實說,有些看你的人說,你的臉沒力量使愛呻吟;

passages.original:
To say they err I dare not be so bold,
Although I swear it to myself alone.
passages.vernacular: 話他們錯,我唔敢咁大膽,雖然我獨自對自己發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說他們錯,我不敢這樣大膽,雖然我獨自對自己發誓。

passages.original:
And to be sure that is not false I swear,
A thousand groans, but thinking on thy face,
One on another’s neck, do witness bear
Thy black is fairest in my judgement’s place.
passages.vernacular: 為咗肯定那並唔虛假,我發誓,一千聲呻吟,只係想起你嘅臉,一聲接一聲,作證你嘅黑在我判斷嘅位置上最美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了肯定那並不虛假,我發誓,一千聲呻吟,只是想起你的臉,一聲接一聲,作證你的黑在我判斷的位置上最美。

passages.original:
In nothing art thou black save in thy deeds,
And thence this slander, as I think, proceeds.
passages.vernacular: 你只在你嘅行為上黑,在其他方面都唔黑,我想這個誹謗從此而來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只在你的行為上黑,在其他方面都不黑,我想這個誹謗從此而來。

passages.title: Sonnet 132
passages.original:
Thine eyes I love, and they, as pitying me,
Knowing thy heart torment me with disdain,
Have put on black and loving mourners be,
Looking with pretty ruth upon my pain.
passages.vernacular: 我愛你嘅眼睛,佢哋好似可憐我,知道你嘅心用蔑視折磨我,穿上黑色,成為有愛嘅哀悼者,用漂亮嘅憐憫望住我嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛你的眼睛,它們好像可憐我,知道你的心用蔑視折磨我,穿上黑色,成為有愛的哀悼者,用漂亮的憐憫望著我的痛苦。

passages.original:
And truly not the morning sun of heaven
Better becomes the grey cheeks of the east,
Nor that full star that ushers in the even,
Doth half that glory to the sober west,
As those two mourning eyes become thy face:
passages.vernacular: 真係,天上嘅朝陽唔會比佢更配東方灰色嘅臉頰,引入黃昏嘅圓滿之星,亦唔會將一半嗰種榮耀畀肅穆嘅西方,好似你臉上呢兩隻哀悼嘅眼睛咁配:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的,天上的朝陽不會比它更配東方灰色的臉頰,引入黃昏的圓滿之星,也不會將一半那種榮耀給肅穆的西方,像你臉上這兩隻哀悼的眼睛那樣配:

passages.original:
O! let it then as well beseem thy heart
To mourn for me since mourning doth thee grace,
And suit thy pity like in every part.
passages.vernacular: 啊!咁就讓你嘅心也同樣合適,為我哀悼,因為哀悼為你增光,令你嘅憐憫在每個部分都相配。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!那就讓你的心也同樣合適,為我哀悼,因為哀悼為你增光,使你的憐憫在每個部分都相配。

passages.original:
Then will I swear beauty herself is black,
And all they foul that thy complexion lack.
passages.vernacular: 那時我會發誓美貌本身係黑,而所有欠缺你膚色嘅都醜陋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時我會發誓美貌本身是黑,而所有欠缺你膚色的都醜陋。

passages.title: Sonnet 133
passages.original:
Beshrew that heart that makes my heart to groan
For that deep wound it gives my friend and me!
passages.vernacular: 詛咒嗰顆令我嘅心呻吟嘅心,因為佢畀我朋友同我帶嚟咁深嘅傷口!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 詛咒那顆使我的心呻吟的心,因為她給我朋友和我帶來這麼深的傷口!

passages.original:
Is’t not enough to torture me alone,
But slave to slavery my sweet’st friend must be?
passages.vernacular: 獨自折磨我仲唔夠嗎,我最甜美嘅朋友都必須淪為奴役嘅奴隸?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獨自折磨我還不夠嗎,我最甜美的朋友也必須淪為奴役的奴隸?

passages.original:
Me from myself thy cruel eye hath taken,
And my next self thou harder hast engross’d:
passages.vernacular: 你殘酷嘅眼睛將我從自己身邊奪走,你更狠咁霸佔咗我嘅另一個自己:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你殘酷的眼睛將我從自己身邊奪走,你更狠地霸佔了我的另一個自己:

passages.original: Of him, myself, and thee I am forsaken;
passages.vernacular: 我被佢、我自己同你拋棄;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被他、我自己和你拋棄;

passages.original: A torment thrice three-fold thus to be cross’d:
passages.vernacular: 就咁被三重三倍嘅折磨所阻撓:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣被三重三倍的折磨所阻撓:

passages.original:
Prison my heart in thy steel bosom’s ward,
But then my friend’s heart let my poor heart bail;
passages.vernacular: 將我嘅心囚禁喺你鋼鐵胸膛嘅牢房,不過然後讓我可憐嘅心保釋我朋友嘅心;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將我的心囚禁在你鋼鐵胸膛的牢房,不過然後讓我可憐的心保釋我朋友的心;

passages.original: Whoe’er keeps me, let my heart be his guard;
passages.vernacular: 無論邊個看守我,讓我嘅心做佢嘅守衛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論誰看守我,讓我的心做他的守衛;

passages.original: Thou canst not then use rigour in my jail:
passages.vernacular: 咁你就唔能夠喺我嘅監獄使用嚴酷:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你就不能夠在我的監獄使用嚴酷:

passages.original:
And yet thou wilt; for I, being pent in thee,
Perforce am thine, and all that is in me.
passages.vernacular: 然而你會;因為我被關喺你裡面,不由自主屬於你,連同我身上一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而你會;因為我被關在你裡面,不由自主屬於你,連同我身上一切。

passages.title: Sonnet 134
passages.original:
So, now I have confess’d that he is thine,
And I my self am mortgag’d to thy will,
Myself I’ll forfeit, so that other mine
Thou wilt restore to be my comfort still:
passages.vernacular: 所以,我而家已承認佢係你嘅,而我自己被抵押畀你嘅意志,我會放棄我自己,好令你將另一個我嘅,仍然交還作我嘅安慰:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,我現在已承認他是你的,而我自己被抵押給你的意志,我會放棄我自己,好使你將另一個我的,仍然交還作我的安慰:

passages.original:
But thou wilt not, nor he will not be free,
For thou art covetous, and he is kind;
passages.vernacular: 不過你唔會,佢亦唔會自由,因為你貪婪,而佢仁慈;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過你不會,他也不會自由,因為你貪婪,而他仁慈;

passages.original:
He learn’d but surety-like to write for me,
Under that bond that him as fast doth bind.
passages.vernacular: 佢只學咗好似擔保人咁為我簽名,在嗰份同樣牢牢綁住佢嘅契約下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只學了像擔保人那樣為我簽名,在那份同樣牢牢綁住他的契約下。

passages.vernacular: 你會取你美貌嘅法規,你呢個放高利貸者,將所有都拿出去生息,並起訴為我而成為債務人嘅朋友;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會取你美貌的法規,你這個放高利貸者,將所有都拿出去生息,並起訴為我而成為債務人的朋友;

passages.original: So him I lose through my unkind abuse.
passages.vernacular: 所以我因我不友善嘅濫用而失去佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我因我不友善的濫用而失去他。

passages.original: Him have I lost; thou hast both him and me:
passages.vernacular: 我已失去佢;你擁有佢同我:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已失去他;你擁有他和我:

passages.original: He pays the whole, and yet am I not free.
passages.vernacular: 佢支付全部,而我仍未自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他支付全部,而我仍未自由。

passages.title: Sonnet 135
passages.original:
Whoever hath her wish, thou hast thy ‘Will,’
And ‘Will’ to boot, and ‘Will’ in over-plus;
passages.vernacular: 無論邊個有佢嘅願望,你都有你嘅「Will」(既係意願,亦係名字威爾),仲有額外嘅「Will」,同過剩嘅「Will」;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論誰有他的願望,你都有你的「Will」(既是意願,也是名字威爾),還有額外的「Will」,和過剩的「Will」;

passages.original:
More than enough am I that vex’d thee still,
To thy sweet will making addition thus.
passages.vernacular: 我多過足夠,一直煩擾你,就咁喺你甜美嘅意願上增加:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我多過足夠,一直煩擾你,就這樣在你甜美的意願上增加:

passages.original:
Wilt thou, whose will is large and spacious,
Not once vouchsafe to hide my will in thine?
passages.vernacular: 你,意願廣闊寬大,冇一次肯將我嘅意願藏喺你嘅意願中嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,意願廣闊寬大,沒一次肯將我的意願藏在你的意願中嗎?

passages.original:
Shall will in others seem right gracious,
And in my will no fair acceptance shine?
passages.vernacular: 意願在別人身上顯得好優雅,而在我嘅意願上就冇美好嘅接納閃耀?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 意願在別人身上顯得很優雅,而在我的意願上就沒美好的接納閃耀?

passages.original:
The sea, all water, yet receives rain still,
And in abundance addeth to his store;
passages.vernacular: 海,全部係水,仍然接受雨,並喺豐盛中增加佢嘅儲備;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海,全部是水,仍然接受雨,並在豐盛中增加他的儲備;

passages.original:
So thou, being rich in ‘Will,’ add to thy ‘Will’
One will of mine, to make thy large will more.
passages.vernacular: 所以你,富於「Will」,將我嘅一個意願加到你嘅「Will」上,令你嘅大意願更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你,富於「Will」,將我的一個意願加到你的「Will」上,使你的大意願更多。

passages.original: Let no unkind ‘No’ fair beseechers kill;
passages.vernacular: 唔好讓不友善嘅「唔」殺死美好嘅懇求者;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要讓不友善的「不」殺死美好的懇求者;

passages.original: Think all but one, and me in that one ‘Will.’
passages.vernacular: 將全部當作一個,而我就在嗰個「Will」之中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將全部當作一個,而我就在那個「Will」之中。

passages.title: Sonnet 136
passages.vernacular: 如果你嘅靈魂責備你,話我靠得咁近,就對你盲目嘅靈魂發誓我係你嘅「Will」,而意願,你嘅靈魂知道,係獲准入嗰度嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你的靈魂責備你,說我靠得這麼近,就對你盲目的靈魂發誓我是你的「Will」,而意願,你的靈魂知道,是獲准進那裡的;

passages.original: Thus far for love, my love-suit, sweet, fulfil.
passages.vernacular: 到此為止為咗愛,我嘅愛情請求,甜蜜嘅,請成全。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到此為止為了愛,我的愛情請求,甜蜜的,請成全。

passages.original:
‘Will’, will fulfil the treasure of thy love,
Ay, fill it full with wills, and my will one.
passages.vernacular: 「Will」會充滿你愛嘅寶庫,係,用意願將佢填滿,而我嘅意願係其中一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「Will」會充滿你愛的寶庫,是,用意願將它填滿,而我的意願是其中一個。

passages.original:
In things of great receipt with ease we prove
Among a number one is reckon’d none:
passages.vernacular: 在容量巨大嘅事物中,我哋輕易證明,在一大堆之中,一個被算作無:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在容量巨大的事物中,我們輕易證明,在一大堆之中,一個被算作無:

passages.original:
Then in the number let me pass untold,
Though in thy store’s account I one must be;
passages.vernacular: 咁就讓我喺數目中不被計算地通過,雖然在你寶庫嘅賬目上,我必須係一個;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就讓我在數目中不被計算地通過,雖然在你寶庫的賬目上,我必須是一個;

passages.original:
For nothing hold me, so it please thee hold
That nothing me, a something sweet to thee:
passages.vernacular: 視我為無,只要你樂意持有嗰個「無」,我,對你甜蜜嘅「有」:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 視我為無,只要你樂意持有那個「無」,我,對你甜蜜的「有」:

passages.original:
Make but my name thy love, and love that still,
And then thou lov’st me for my name is ‘Will.’
passages.vernacular: 只要將我嘅名字當作你嘅愛,並一直愛佢,咁你就愛我,因為我嘅名字係「威爾」(Will)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要將我的名字當作你的愛,並一直愛它,那你就愛我,因為我的名字是「威爾」(Will)。

passages.title: Sonnet 137
passages.original:
Thou blind fool, Love, what dost thou to mine eyes,
That they behold, and see not what they see?
passages.vernacular: 你呢個盲目嘅傻瓜,愛,你對我嘅眼睛做咗咩,令佢哋望見,卻睇唔到佢哋所見?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這個盲目的傻瓜,愛,你對我的眼睛做了什麼,使它們望見,卻看不到它們所見?

passages.original:
They know what beauty is, see where it lies,
Yet what the best is take the worst to be.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋知道美係咩,見到佢喺邊,卻將最好嘅當作最壞;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們知道美是什麼,看到它在哪,卻將最好的當作最壞;

passages.original:
If eyes, corrupt by over-partial looks,
Be anchor’d in the bay where all men ride,
Why of eyes’ falsehood hast thou forged hooks,
Whereto the judgement of my heart is tied?
passages.vernacular: 如果被過分偏袒嘅目光腐蝕嘅眼睛,停泊喺所有人都騎行嘅海灣,你點解用眼睛嘅虛假鍛造鉤子,將我心嘅判斷綁在上面?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果被過分偏袒的目光腐蝕的眼睛,停泊在所有人都騎行的海灣,你為什麼用眼睛的虛假鍛造鉤子,將我心的判斷綁在上面?

passages.original:
Why should my heart think that a several plot,
Which my heart knows the wide world’s common place?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心點解要認為嗰塊係專屬嘅地,而我嘅心知道佢係廣闊世界嘅公共地?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心為什麼要認為那塊是專屬的地,而我的心知道它是廣闊世界的公共地?

passages.original:
Or mine eyes, seeing this, say this is not,
To put fair truth upon so foul a face?
passages.vernacular: 或者我嘅眼睛看到呢個,點解講呢個唔係,將美好嘅真放在咁醜陋嘅臉上?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者我的眼睛看到這個,為什麼說這個不是,將美好的真放在這麼醜陋的臉上?

passages.original:
In things right true my heart and eyes have err’d,
And to this false plague are they now transferr’d.
passages.vernacular: 在非常正確嘅事上,我嘅心同眼睛都錯了,而佢哋而家被轉移到呢個虛假嘅瘟疫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在非常正確的事上,我的心和眼睛都錯了,而它們現在被轉移到這個虛假的瘟疫。

passages.title: Sonnet 138
passages.original:
When my love swears that she is made of truth,
I do believe her though I know she lies,
That she might think me some untutor’d youth,
Unlearned in the world’s false subtleties.
passages.vernacular: 當我嘅愛人發誓佢係由真造成,我相信佢,雖然我知道佢撒謊,好令佢可能認為我係個未受教導嘅青年,對世界虛假嘅微妙一無所知。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我的愛人發誓她是由真造成,我相信她,雖然我知道她撒謊,好使她可能認為我是個未受教導的青年,對世界虛假的微妙一無所知。

passages.original:
Thus vainly thinking that she thinks me young,
Although she knows my days are past the best,
Simply I credit her false-speaking tongue:
passages.vernacular: 就咁徒勞地以為佢以為我年輕,雖然佢知道我嘅日子已過咗最好,我單純地相信佢虛假說話嘅舌頭:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣徒勞地以為她以為我年輕,雖然她知道我的日子已過了最好,我單純地相信她虛假說話的舌頭:

passages.original: On both sides thus is simple truth suppressed:
passages.vernacular: 雙方就咁壓抑咗單純嘅真:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雙方就這樣壓抑了單純的真:

passages.original: But wherefore says she not she is unjust?
passages.vernacular: 不過佢點解唔講佢唔忠?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她為什麼不說她不忠?

passages.original: And wherefore say not I that I am old?
passages.vernacular: 我點解唔講我老?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為什麼不說我老?

passages.original:
O! love’s best habit is in seeming trust,
And age in love, loves not to have years told:
passages.vernacular: 啊!愛最好嘅習慣係在似是信任中,而年老嘅愛,唔愛數年歲:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!愛最好的習慣是在似是信任中,而年老的愛,不愛數年歲:

passages.original:
Therefore I lie with her, and she with me,
And in our faults by lies we flatter’d be.
passages.vernacular: 所以我同佢撒謊,佢同我撒謊,喺我哋嘅過失中,我哋被謊言奉承。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我與她撒謊,她與我撒謊,在我們的過失中,我們被謊言奉承。

passages.title: Sonnet 139
passages.original:
O! call not me to justify the wrong
That thy unkindness lays upon my heart;
passages.vernacular: 啊!唔好叫我為你嘅不友善放在我心上嘅錯去辯護;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!不要叫我為你的不友善放在我心上的錯去辯護;

passages.original: Wound me not with thine eye, but with thy tongue:
passages.vernacular: 唔好用你嘅眼睛傷我,而係用你嘅舌頭:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要用你的眼睛傷我,而是用你的舌頭:

passages.original:
Use power with power, and slay me not by art,
Tell me thou lov’st elsewhere; but in my sight,
Dear heart, forbear to glance thine eye aside:
passages.vernacular: 以力量對力量,唔好用技巧殺我,告訴我你愛別處;不過喺我視線之內,親愛嘅心,唔好將你嘅眼睛瞥向一邊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以力量對力量,不要用技巧殺我,告訴我你愛別處;不過在我視線之內,親愛的心,不要將你的眼睛瞥向一邊:

passages.original:
What need’st thou wound with cunning, when thy might
Is more than my o’erpress’d defence can bide?
passages.vernacular: 當你嘅力量大過我受壓過度嘅防禦所能承受,你需要用狡猾傷我做咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你的力量大過我受壓過度的防禦所能承受,你需要用狡猾傷我做什麼?

passages.original:
Let me excuse thee: ah! my love well knows
Her pretty looks have been mine enemies;
passages.vernacular: 讓我為你辯解:啊!我嘅愛人清楚知道,佢漂亮嘅神情一直係我嘅敵人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我為你辯解:啊!我的愛人清楚知道,她漂亮的神情一直是我的敵人;

passages.original:
And therefore from my face she turns my foes,
That they elsewhere might dart their injuries:
passages.vernacular: 所以佢將我嘅敵人從我嘅臉轉開,好令佢哋喺別處射出佢哋嘅傷害:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她將我的敵人從我的臉轉開,好使他們在別處射出他們的傷害:

passages.original:
Yet do not so; but since I am near slain,
Kill me outright with looks, and rid my pain.
passages.vernacular: 不過唔好咁做;不過既然我差唔多被殺,就直接用神情殺死我,解除我嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過不要這樣做;不過既然我差不多被殺,就直接用神情殺死我,解除我的痛苦。

passages.title: Sonnet 140
passages.original:
Be wise as thou art cruel; do not press
My tongue-tied patience with too much disdain;
passages.vernacular: 你要同你殘忍一樣聰明;唔好用太多蔑視壓迫我啞口嘅耐性;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要和你殘忍一樣聰明;不要用太多蔑視壓迫我啞口的耐性;

passages.original:
Lest sorrow lend me words, and words express
The manner of my pity-wanting pain.
passages.vernacular: 免得悲傷畀我言辭,而言辭表達我需要憐憫嘅痛苦嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 免得悲傷給我言辭,而言辭表達我需要憐憫的痛苦的方式。

passages.original:
If I might teach thee wit, better it were,
Though not to love, yet love to tell me so,
As testy sick men, when their deaths be near,
No news but health from their physicians know.
passages.vernacular: 如果我可以教你智慧,更好就係,雖然唔愛,都愛講你愛我,好似暴躁嘅病人,臨死時,從醫生嗰度只知道健康嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我可以教你智慧,更好就是,雖然不愛,也愛說你愛我,好像暴躁的病人,臨死時,從醫生那裡只知道健康的消息。

passages.original:
For, if I should despair, I should grow mad,
And in my madness might speak ill of thee;
passages.vernacular: 因為如果我絕望,我會發瘋,喺瘋狂中可能講你壞話;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果我絕望,我會發瘋,在瘋狂中可能說你壞話;

passages.original:
Now this ill-wresting world is grown so bad,
Mad slanderers by mad ears believed be.
passages.vernacular: 而家呢個惡意曲解嘅世界變得咁壞,瘋狂嘅誹謗者被瘋狂嘅耳朵相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在這個惡意曲解的世界變得這麼壞,瘋狂的誹謗者被瘋狂的耳朵相信。

passages.original:
That I may not be so, nor thou belied,
Bear thine eyes straight, though thy proud heart go wide.
passages.vernacular: 為咗令我唔會咁,你亦唔被誣蔑,將你嘅眼睛擺正,雖然你驕傲嘅心走偏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了使我不會這樣,你也不被誣蔑,將你的眼睛擺正,雖然你驕傲的心走偏。

passages.title: Sonnet 141
passages.original:
In faith I do not love thee with mine eyes,
For they in thee a thousand errors note;
passages.vernacular: 老實講,我唔係用我嘅眼睛愛你,因為佢哋在你身上察覺一千個錯誤;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老實說,我不是用我的眼睛愛你,因為它們在你身上察覺一千個錯誤;

passages.original:
But ’tis my heart that loves what they despise,
Who, in despite of view, is pleased to dote.
passages.vernacular: 而係我嘅心愛佢哋鄙視嘅,佢不顧視覺,樂意癡迷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而是我的心愛它們鄙視的,他不顧視覺,樂意癡迷。

passages.original: Nor are mine ears with thy tongue’s tune delighted;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅耳朵亦唔因你舌頭嘅曲調而歡喜;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的耳朵也不因你舌頭的曲調而歡喜;

passages.original:
Nor tender feeling, to base touches prone,
Nor taste, nor smell, desire to be invited
To any sensual feast with thee alone:
passages.vernacular: 溫柔嘅感覺,傾向卑賤嘅觸碰,亦唔係味覺、嗅覺,渴望被邀請獨自同你赴任何肉慾嘅盛宴:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫柔的感覺,傾向卑賤的觸碰,也不是味覺、嗅覺,渴望被邀請獨自與你赴任何肉慾的盛宴:

passages.original:
But my five wits nor my five senses can
Dissuade one foolish heart from serving thee,
Who leaves unsway’d the likeness of a man,
Thy proud heart’s slave and vassal wretch to be:
passages.vernacular: 不過我嘅五種智力同五種感覺都唔能夠勸阻一顆愚蠢嘅心去服侍你,佢令一個男人嘅樣子不受擺佈,成為你驕傲心嘅奴隸同可憐嘅家臣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我的五種智力和五種感覺都不能夠勸阻一顆愚蠢的心去服侍你,他使一個男人的樣子不受擺佈,成為你驕傲心的奴隸和可憐的家臣:

passages.original:
Only my plague thus far I count my gain,
That she that makes me sin awards me pain.
passages.vernacular: 到此為止我只算我嘅瘟疫為收穫,即令我犯罪嘅佢賜我痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到此為止我只算我的瘟疫為收穫,即使我犯罪的她賜我痛苦。

passages.title: Sonnet 142
passages.original:
Love is my sin, and thy dear virtue hate,
Hate of my sin, grounded on sinful loving:
passages.vernacular: 愛係我嘅罪,而你親愛嘅美德係恨,對我罪嘅恨,建基於有罪嘅愛:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛是我的罪,而你親愛的美德是恨,對我罪的恨,建基於有罪的愛:

passages.original:
O! but with mine compare thou thine own state,
And thou shalt find it merits not reproving;
passages.vernacular: 啊!不過用我嘅同你自己嘅狀態比較,你會發現佢唔值得責備;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!不過用我的與你自己的狀態比較,你會發現它不值得責備;

passages.original:
Or, if it do, not from those lips of thine,
That have profan’d their scarlet ornaments
And seal’d false bonds of love as oft as mine,
Robb’d others’ beds’ revenues of their rents.
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果值得,都唔應該從你嗰雙嘴唇,佢哋褻瀆咗佢哋猩紅嘅裝飾,並同我一樣經常蓋上虛假愛嘅契約,搶劫別人床鋪收益嘅租金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果值得,也不應該從你那雙嘴唇,它們褻瀆了它們猩紅的裝飾,並和我一樣經常蓋上虛假愛的契約,搶劫別人床鋪收益的租金。

passages.original:
Be it lawful I love thee, as thou lov’st those
Whom thine eyes woo as mine importune thee:
passages.vernacular: 讓我愛你係合法嘅,正如你愛嗰啲你眼睛求愛嘅人,好似我纏住你:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我愛你是合法的,正如你愛那些你眼睛求愛的人,好像我纏著你:

passages.original:
Root pity in thy heart, that, when it grows,
Thy pity may deserve to pitied be.
passages.vernacular: 將憐憫紮根喺你心中,當佢生長,你嘅憐憫可能值得被憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將憐憫紮根在你心中,當它生長,你的憐憫可能值得被憐憫。

passages.original:
If thou dost seek to have what thou dost hide,
By self-example mayst thou be denied!
passages.vernacular: 如果你尋求擁有你所隱藏嘅,以你自己嘅榜樣,願你被拒絕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你尋求擁有你所隱藏的,以你自己的榜樣,願你被拒絕!

passages.title: Sonnet 143
passages.original:
Lo, as a careful housewife runs to catch
One of her feather’d creatures broke away,
Sets down her babe, and makes all swift dispatch
In pursuit of the thing she would have stay;
passages.vernacular: 看,好似小心嘅家庭主婦跑去捉其中一隻掙脫嘅有羽毛嘅牲口,放低她嘅嬰兒,迅速處理,追逐佢想留住嘅東西;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,好像小心的家庭主婦跑去抓其中一隻掙脫的有羽毛的牲口,放下她的嬰兒,迅速處理,追逐她想留住的東西;

passages.original:
Whilst her neglected child holds her in chase,
Cries to catch her whose busy care is bent
To follow that which flies before her face,
Not prizing her poor infant’s discontent;
passages.vernacular: 而被忽略嘅孩子追趕佢,哭喊著想捉住佢,佢忙碌嘅關注一心追隨喺佢面前飛走嘅東西,唔重視可憐嬰兒嘅不滿;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而被忽略的孩子追趕她,哭喊著想抓住她,她忙碌的關注一心追隨在她面前飛走的東西,不重視可憐嬰兒的不滿;

passages.original:
So runn’st thou after that which flies from thee,
Whilst I thy babe chase thee afar behind;
passages.vernacular: 你也一樣追逐從你飛走嘅,而我,你嘅嬰兒,遠遠喺後面追你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也一樣追逐從你飛走的,而我,你的嬰兒,遠遠在後面追你;

passages.original:
But if thou catch thy hope, turn back to me,
And play the mother’s part, kiss me, be kind;
passages.vernacular: 不過如果你捉到你嘅希望,就返嚟我身邊,扮演母親嘅角色,吻我,仁慈啲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過如果你抓到你的希望,就回到我身邊,扮演母親的角色,吻我,仁慈些;

passages.original:
So will I pray that thou mayst have thy ‘Will,’
If thou turn back and my loud crying still.
passages.vernacular: 咁我會祈求你得到你嘅「Will」,如果你轉身返嚟並平息我嘅大聲哭喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我會祈求你得到你的「Will」,如果你轉身回來並平息我的大聲哭喊。

passages.title: Sonnet 144
passages.original:
Two loves I have of comfort and despair,
Which like two spirits do suggest me still:
passages.vernacular: 我有兩份愛,一份係安慰,一份係絕望,好似兩個靈魂一直向我提示:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有兩份愛,一份是安慰,一份是絕望,好像兩個靈魂一直向我提示:

passages.original:
The better angel is a man right fair,
The worser spirit a woman colour’d ill.
passages.vernacular: 較好嘅天使係個非常俊美嘅男人,較壞嘅靈魂係個膚色不佳嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 較好的天使是個非常俊美的男人,較壞的靈魂是個膚色不佳的女人。

passages.original:
To win me soon to hell, my female evil,
Tempteth my better angel from my side,
And would corrupt my saint to be a devil,
Wooing his purity with her foul pride.
passages.vernacular: 為咗好快將我贏去地獄,我嘅女性之惡,將我較好嘅天使從我身邊誘走,想敗壞我嘅聖人成為魔鬼,用佢污穢嘅驕傲向佢嘅純潔求愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了很快將我贏去地獄,我的女性之惡,將我較好的天使從我身邊誘走,想敗壞我的聖人成為魔鬼,用她污穢的驕傲向他的純潔求愛。

passages.original:
And whether that my angel be turn’d fiend,
Suspect I may, yet not directly tell;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅天使會唔會變成惡魔,我可能懷疑,卻唔能直接講出;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的天使會不會變成惡魔,我可能懷疑,卻不能直接說出;

passages.original:
But being both from me, both to each friend,
I guess one angel in another’s hell:
passages.vernacular: 不過兩者都離開我,彼此成為朋友,我猜一個天使在另一個嘅地獄中:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過兩者都離開我,彼此成為朋友,我猜一個天使在另一個的地獄中:

passages.original:
Yet this shall I ne’er know, but live in doubt,
Till my bad angel fire my good one out.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢個我永遠唔會知道,只能活喺懷疑中,直到我嘅壞天使將我嘅好天使燒出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這個我永遠不會知道,只能活在懷疑中,直到我的壞天使將我的好天使燒出來。

passages.title: Sonnet 145
passages.original:
Those lips that Love’s own hand did make,
Breathed forth the sound that said ‘I hate’,
To me that languish’d for her sake:
passages.vernacular: 嗰雙由愛神自己手造嘅嘴唇,呼出話「我恨」嘅聲音,對我(為佢憔悴嘅人):
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那雙由愛神自己手造的嘴唇,呼出說「我恨」的聲音,對我(為她憔悴的人):

passages.original:
But when she saw my woeful state,
Straight in her heart did mercy come,
Chiding that tongue that ever sweet
Was us’d in giving gentle doom;
passages.vernacular: 不過當佢見到我悲慘嘅狀態,憐憫即刻喺佢心中升起,責備嗰條舌頭,佢一直甜美地用來宣布溫柔嘅判決;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當她看到我悲慘的狀態,憐憫立刻在她心中升起,責備那條舌頭,她一直甜美地用來宣布溫柔的判決;

passages.original: And taught it thus anew to greet;
passages.vernacular: 並教佢咁重新問候;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並教她這樣重新問候;

passages.original:
‘I hate’ she alter’d with an end,
That followed it as gentle day,
Doth follow night, who like a fiend
From heaven to hell is flown away.
passages.vernacular: 佢用一個結尾改變咗「我恨」,嗰個結尾好似溫柔嘅白晝跟住夜晚,夜晚好似惡魔從天堂飛去地獄:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用一個結尾改變了「我恨」,那個結尾好像溫柔的白晝跟著夜晚,夜晚好像惡魔從天堂飛去地獄:

passages.original:
‘I hate’, from hate away she threw,
And sav’d my life, saying ‘not you’.
passages.vernacular: 「我恨」,佢將恨拋開,救咗我嘅命,講「唔係你」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恨」,她將恨拋開,救了我的命,說「不是你」。

passages.title: Sonnet 146
passages.original:
Poor soul, the centre of my sinful earth,
My sinful earth these rebel powers array,
Why dost thou pine within and suffer dearth,
Painting thy outward walls so costly gay?
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅靈魂,我有罪嘅大地嘅中心,我有罪嘅大地,呢啲叛逆嘅力量嘅陣列,你點解喺內裡憔悴受匱乏之苦,卻將你嘅外牆塗得咁昂貴華麗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的靈魂,我有罪的大地的中心,我有罪的大地,這些叛逆的力量的陣列,你為什麼在內裡憔悴受匱乏之苦,卻將你的外牆塗得這麼昂貴華麗?

passages.original:
Why so large cost, having so short a lease,
Dost thou upon thy fading mansion spend?
passages.vernacular: 租期咁短,你點解喺你正在褪色嘅大宅上花咁大嘅費用?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 租期這麼短,你為什麼在你正在褪色的大宅上花這麼大的費用?

passages.original:
Shall worms, inheritors of this excess,
Eat up thy charge? Is this thy body’s end?
passages.vernacular: 蛆蟲,呢種過度嘅繼承人,會吃掉你嘅花費嗎?呢個就係你身體嘅終點?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蛆蟲,這種過度的繼承人,會吃掉你的花費嗎?這個就是你身體的終點?

passages.original:
Then soul, live thou upon thy servant’s loss,
And let that pine to aggravate thy store;
passages.vernacular: 咁靈魂,靠你僕人嘅損失生活,讓佢憔悴,好增加你嘅儲備;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那靈魂,靠你僕人的損失生活,讓他憔悴,好增加你的儲備;

passages.original: Buy terms divine in selling hours of dross;
passages.vernacular: 出賣糟粕嘅時辰,買取神聖嘅期限;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出賣糟粕的時辰,買取神聖的期限;

passages.original: Within be fed, without be rich no more:
passages.vernacular: 內裡被餵養,外面唔再富有:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 內裡被餵養,外面不再富有:

passages.original:
So shall thou feed on Death, that feeds on men,
And Death once dead, there’s no more dying then.
passages.vernacular: 咁你就食死亡,死亡食人,而死亡一旦死去,就冇更多嘅死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣你就吃死亡,死亡吃人,而死亡一旦死去,就沒更多的死。

passages.title: Sonnet 147
passages.original:
My love is as a fever longing still,
For that which longer nurseth the disease;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅愛好似發燒,一直渴求更長久滋養疾病嘅東西;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的愛好像發燒,一直渴求更長久滋養疾病的東西;

passages.original:
Feeding on that which doth preserve the ill,
The uncertain sickly appetite to please.
passages.vernacular: 以保存病痛嘅東西為食,取悅不確定嘅病態食慾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以保存病痛的東西為食,取悅不確定的病態食慾。

passages.original:
My reason, the physician to my love,
Angry that his prescriptions are not kept,
Hath left me, and I desperate now approve
Desire is death, which physic did except.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅理性,我愛嘅醫生,憤怒佢嘅處方冇被遵守,已離開我,而我絕望地現在證實:慾望係死亡,而藥物曾排除佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的理性,我愛的醫生,憤怒他的處方沒被遵守,已離開我,而我絕望地現在證實:慾望是死亡,而藥物曾排除它。

passages.original:
Past cure I am, now Reason is past care,
And frantic-mad with evermore unrest;
passages.vernacular: 我無可救藥,而家理性不再關心,我因永無休止嘅不安而瘋狂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無可救藥,現在理性不再關心,我因永無休止的不安而瘋狂;

passages.original:
My thoughts and my discourse as madmen’s are,
At random from the truth vainly express’d;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅思想同談話好似瘋子,隨意徒勞地離開真理而表達;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的思想和談話好像瘋子,隨意徒勞地離開真理而表達;

passages.original:
For I have sworn thee fair, and thought thee bright,
Who art as black as hell, as dark as night.
passages.vernacular: 因為我發誓你美,以為你明亮,而你黑得似地獄,暗得似夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我發誓你美,以為你明亮,而你黑得像地獄,暗得像夜晚。

passages.title: Sonnet 148
passages.original:
O me! what eyes hath Love put in my head,
Which have no correspondence with true sight;
passages.vernacular: 唉!愛神喺我頭上放咗啲咩眼睛,同真正嘅視覺冇對應;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉!愛神在我頭上放了些什麼眼睛,與真正的視覺沒對應;

passages.original:
Or, if they have, where is my judgement fled,
That censures falsely what they see aright?
passages.vernacular: 或者,如果有,我嘅判斷逃咗去邊,錯誤咁批評佢哋正確見到嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,如果有,我的判斷逃去了哪,錯誤地批評它們正確看到的?

passages.original:
If that be fair whereon my false eyes dote,
What means the world to say it is not so?
passages.vernacular: 如果我虛假嘅眼睛癡迷嘅係美,世界點解講唔係咁?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我虛假的眼睛癡迷的是美,世界為什麼說不是這樣?

passages.original:
If it be not, then love doth well denote
Love’s eye is not so true as all men’s: no,
How can it? O! how can Love’s eye be true,
That is so vexed with watching and with tears?
passages.vernacular: 如果唔係,咁愛清楚表明愛嘅眼睛唔似所有人嘅咁真:唔,佢點可能?啊!被守夜同眼淚咁困擾嘅愛嘅眼睛,點可能真?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不是,那愛清楚表明愛的眼睛不像所有人的這麼真:不,它怎可能?啊!被守夜和眼淚這麼困擾的愛的眼睛,怎可能真?

passages.original: No marvel then, though I mistake my view;
passages.vernacular: 咁我弄錯我嘅視野也唔奇怪;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我弄錯我的視野也不奇怪;

passages.original: The sun itself sees not, till heaven clears.
passages.vernacular: 連太陽本身都睇唔到,直到天放晴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連太陽本身都看不到,直到天放晴。

passages.original:
O cunning Love! with tears thou keep’st me blind,
Lest eyes well-seeing thy foul faults should find.
passages.vernacular: 啊狡猾嘅愛!你用眼淚令我保持失明,免得好眼睛發現你醜陋嘅過失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊狡猾的愛!你用眼淚使我保持失明,免得好眼睛發現你醜陋的過失。

passages.title: Sonnet 149
passages.original:
Canst thou, O cruel! say I love thee not,
When I against myself with thee partake?
passages.vernacular: 你,啊殘忍嘅,可以講我唔愛你,當我為你同我自己作對?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,啊殘忍的,可以說我不愛你,當我為你與我自己作對?

passages.original:
Do I not think on thee, when I forgot
Am of my self, all tyrant, for thy sake?
passages.vernacular: 我唔係想你,當我為你嘅緣故,完全暴君般咁忘記自己?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是想你,當我為你的緣故,完全暴君般地忘記自己?

passages.original:
Who hateth thee that I do call my friend,
On whom frown’st thou that I do fawn upon,
Nay, if thou lour’st on me, do I not spend
Revenge upon myself with present moan?
passages.vernacular: 邊個恨你,我就稱為朋友,你對邊個皺眉,我就向邊個諂媚,不,如果你對我怒目,我唔係用即時嘅呻吟對自己報復嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰恨你,我就稱為朋友,你對誰皺眉,我就向誰諂媚,不,如果你對我怒目,我不是用即時的呻吟對自己報復嗎?

passages.original:
What merit do I in my self respect,
That is so proud thy service to despise,
When all my best doth worship thy defect,
Commanded by the motion of thine eyes?
passages.vernacular: 我喺自己身上尊重咩功績,咁驕傲以致鄙視你嘅服務,當我所有最好嘅都崇拜你嘅缺點,受你眼睛嘅動作指揮?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在自己身上尊重什麼功績,這麼驕傲以致鄙視你的服務,當我所有最好的都崇拜你的缺點,受你眼睛的動作指揮?

passages.original: But, love, hate on, for now I know thy mind;
passages.vernacular: 不過,愛人,繼續恨吧,因為我而家知道你嘅心思;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,愛人,繼續恨吧,因為我現在知道你的心思;

passages.original: Those that can see thou lov’st, and I am blind.
passages.vernacular: 你愛嗰啲看得見嘅人,而我係盲嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你愛那些看得見的人,而我是盲的。

passages.title: Sonnet 150
passages.original:
O! from what power hast thou this powerful might,
With insufficiency my heart to sway?
passages.vernacular: 啊!你從咩力量得到呢種有力嘅力量,用不足去擺佈我嘅心?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!你從什麼力量得到這種有力的力量,用不足去擺佈我的心?

passages.original:
To make me give the lie to my true sight,
And swear that brightness doth not grace the day?
passages.vernacular: 令我否認我真正嘅視覺,發誓光明並唔點綴白晝?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使我否認我真正的視覺,發誓光明並不點綴白晝?

passages.original:
Whence hast thou this becoming of things ill,
That in the very refuse of thy deeds
There is such strength and warrantise of skill,
That, in my mind, thy worst all best exceeds?
passages.vernacular: 你從邊度得到將壞事變得相稱嘅能力,以致在你行為嘅渣滓裡,有咁大嘅力量同技巧嘅保證,令你最壞嘅,在我心中超越所有最好嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從哪裡得到將壞事變得相稱的能力,以致在你行為的渣滓裡,有這麼大的力量和技巧的保證,使你最壞的,在我心中超越所有最好的?

passages.original:
Who taught thee how to make me love thee more,
The more I hear and see just cause of hate?
passages.vernacular: 邊個教你點樣令我更愛你,我聽到同見到正當恨嘅理由越多?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰教你怎樣使我更愛你,我聽到和看到正當恨的理由越多?

passages.original:
O! though I love what others do abhor,
With others thou shouldst not abhor my state:
passages.vernacular: 啊!雖然我愛別人所憎惡嘅,你唔應該同別人一樣憎惡我嘅狀態:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊!雖然我愛別人所憎惡的,你不應該和別人一樣憎惡我的狀態:

passages.original:
If thy unworthiness rais’d love in me,
More worthy I to be belov’d of thee.
passages.vernacular: 如果你嘅不值令我產生愛,我更值得被你愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你的不值使我產生愛,我更值得被你愛。

passages.title: Sonnet 151
passages.original:
Love is too young to know what conscience is,
Yet who knows not conscience is born of love?
passages.vernacular: 愛太年輕,唔知道良心係咩,然而邊個唔知道良心由愛而生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛太年輕,不知道良心是什麼,然而誰不知道良心由愛而生?

passages.original:
Then, gentle cheater, urge not my amiss,
Lest guilty of my faults thy sweet self prove:
passages.vernacular: 咁,溫柔嘅騙子,唔好催逼我嘅過錯,免得你甜美嘅自己證明係我過失嘅罪人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那,溫柔的騙子,不要催逼我的過錯,免得你甜美的自己證明是我過失的罪人:

passages.original:
For, thou betraying me, I do betray
My nobler part to my gross body’s treason;
passages.vernacular: 因為你背叛我,我背叛我更高貴嘅部分,屈從於我粗劣身體嘅叛變;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你背叛我,我背叛我更高貴的部分,屈從於我粗劣身體的叛變;

passages.original:
My soul doth tell my body that he may
Triumph in love; flesh stays no farther reason,
But rising at thy name doth point out thee,
As his triumphant prize. Proud of this pride,
He is contented thy poor drudge to be,
To stand in thy affairs, fall by thy side.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅靈魂告訴我嘅身體,佢可以在愛中得勝;肉體唔再講理,而係聽到你嘅名字就升起,指出你作為佢得勝嘅獎品。為呢種驕傲而驕傲,佢滿足於做你可憐嘅苦工,在你嘅事務中站起,在你身邊倒下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的靈魂告訴我的身體,他可以在愛中得勝;肉體不再講理,而是聽到你的名字就升起,指出你作為他得勝的獎品。為這種驕傲而驕傲,他滿足於做你可憐的苦工,在你的事務中站起,在你身邊倒下。

passages.original:
No want of conscience hold it that I call
Her ‘love,’ for whose dear love I rise and fall.
passages.vernacular: 唔好認為我欠缺良心,因為我稱「愛」嘅佢,我為佢親愛嘅愛起起落落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要認為我欠缺良心,因為我稱「愛」的她,我為她親愛的愛起起落落。

passages.title: Sonnet 152
passages.original:
In loving thee thou know’st I am forsworn,
But thou art twice forsworn, to me love swearing;
passages.vernacular: 你知道,我愛你就背誓了,不過你背誓兩次,向我發愛嘅誓:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,我愛你就背誓了,不過你背誓兩次,向我發愛的誓:

passages.original:
In act thy bed-vow broke, and new faith torn,
In vowing new hate after new love bearing:
passages.vernacular: 行為上你打破咗床誓,撕毀新信,在新愛之後發新恨嘅誓:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 行為上你打破了床誓,撕毀新信,在新愛之後發新恨的誓:

passages.original:
But why of two oaths’ breach do I accuse thee,
When I break twenty? I am perjur’d most;
passages.vernacular: 不過我點解控告你違反兩個誓,當我違反二十個?我背誓最多;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我為什麼控告你違反兩個誓,當我違反二十個?我背誓最多;

passages.original:
For all my vows are oaths but to misuse thee,
And all my honest faith in thee is lost:
passages.vernacular: 因為我所有嘅誓言只係為咗濫用你嘅誓,而我對你所有誠實嘅信念都失去:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我所有的誓言只是為了濫用你的誓,而我對你所有誠實的信念都失去:

passages.original:
For I have sworn deep oaths of thy deep kindness,
Oaths of thy love, thy truth, thy constancy;
passages.vernacular: 因為我曾對你深深嘅善意發過深誓,對你嘅愛、你嘅真、你嘅恆定發過誓;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我曾對你深深的善意發過深誓,對你的愛、你的真、你的恆定發過誓;

passages.original:
And, to enlighten thee, gave eyes to blindness,
Or made them swear against the thing they see;
passages.vernacular: 為咗啟發你,我畀盲目嘅眼睛,或令佢哋發誓反對佢哋所見嘅東西;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了啟發你,我給盲目的眼睛,或使它們發誓反對它們所見的東西;

passages.original:
For I have sworn thee fair; more perjured I,
To swear against the truth so foul a lie.
passages.vernacular: 因為我發誓你美;我背誓更甚,對真相發誓咁醜陋嘅謊言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我發誓你美;我背誓更甚,對真相發誓這麼醜陋的謊言。

passages.title: Sonnet 153
passages.original: Cupid laid by his brand and fell asleep:
passages.vernacular: 丘比特放低佢嘅火炬,睡著咗:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 丘比特放下他的火炬,睡著了:

passages.vernacular: 狄安娜嘅一個侍女發現呢個機會,即刻將佢點燃愛嘅火浸入嗰處山谷冷泉裡;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狄安娜的一個侍女發現這個機會,立刻將他點燃愛的火浸入那處山谷冷泉裡;

passages.original:
Which borrow’d from this holy fire of Love,
A dateless lively heat, still to endure,
And grew a seething bath, which yet men prove
Against strange maladies a sovereign cure.
passages.vernacular: 泉水從愛嘅神聖火焰借來永不終止嘅活潑熱力,持續不斷,變成沸騰嘅浴池,人們仍然證明佢對奇怪嘅疾病係特效藥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 泉水從愛的神聖火焰借來永不終止的活潑熱力,持續不斷,變成沸騰的浴池,人們仍然證明它對奇怪的疾病是特效藥。

passages.original:
But at my mistress’ eye Love’s brand new-fired,
The boy for trial needs would touch my breast;
passages.vernacular: 不過愛嘅火炬喺我情人嘅眼睛重新點燃,男孩為咗試驗要觸碰我嘅胸膛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過愛的火炬在我情人的眼睛重新點燃,男孩為了試驗要觸碰我的胸膛;

passages.original:
I, sick withal, the help of bath desired,
And thither hied, a sad distemper’d guest,
But found no cure, the bath for my help lies
Where Cupid got new fire; my mistress’ eyes.
passages.vernacular: 我因此生病,想要浴池嘅幫助,匆匆去到嗰度,一個悲傷失調嘅客人,卻找不到治療,浴池幫助我嘅地方,就喺丘比特得到新火嘅地方:我情人嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我因此生病,想要浴池的幫助,匆匆去到那裡,一個悲傷失調的客人,卻找不到治療,浴池幫助我的地方,就在丘比特得到新火的地方:我情人的眼睛。

passages.title: Sonnet 154
passages.original:
The little Love-god lying once asleep,
Laid by his side his heart-inflaming brand,
Whilst many nymphs that vow’d chaste life to keep
Came tripping by; but in her maiden hand
The fairest votary took up that fire
Which many legions of true hearts had warm’d;
passages.vernacular: 小小嘅愛神一度躺住睡著,將佢點燃心嘅火炬放喺身邊,而許多發誓保持貞潔生活嘅仙女輕快經過;不過最美嘅女信徒用佢少女嘅手拿起嗰火,許多軍團嘅真心曾被它溫暖過;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小小的愛神一度躺著睡著,將他點燃心的火炬放在身邊,而許多發誓保持貞潔生活的仙女輕快經過;不過最美的女信徒用她少女的手拿起那火,許多軍團的真心曾被它溫暖過;

passages.original:
And so the general of hot desire
Was, sleeping, by a virgin hand disarm’d.
passages.vernacular: 就咁熾熱慾望嘅統帥,睡著時被一隻處女嘅手繳械。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣熾熱慾望的統帥,睡著時被一隻處女的手繳械。

passages.original:
This brand she quenched in a cool well by,
Which from Love’s fire took heat perpetual,
Growing a bath and healthful remedy,
For men diseased; but I, my mistress’ thrall,
Came there for cure and this by that I prove,
Love’s fire heats water, water cools not love.
passages.vernacular: 佢將呢個火炬浸熄在附近一口涼井,井從愛嘅火取得永久嘅熱力,變成浴池同有益健康嘅療法,畀患病嘅人;不過我,我情人嘅奴隸,去嗰度求治,並憑此證明:愛嘅火令水熱,水唔令愛冷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她將這個火炬浸熄在附近一口涼井,井從愛的火取得永久的熱力,變成浴池和有益健康的療法,給患病的人;不過我,我情人的奴隸,去那裡求治,並憑此證明:愛的火使水熱,水不使愛冷。
